 Hey everyone!   
 I’m a beginner AI automation developer focused on building practical workflows with  n8n, AI/LLM APIs, webhooks, REST APIs, CRM/Google Sheets integrations, and Python . 
 I’m currently looking to work with an  AI automation agency, startup, or business owner  where I can contribute to real projects, learn from production environments, and grow into a strong automation engineer. 
   What I can work with: 
 • n8n workflow automation 
• Webhooks & REST APIs 
• OpenAI / LLM integrations 
• AI classification & qualification 
• Lead routing and processing 
• Google Sheets / CRM workflows 
• Structured AI outputs 
• Conditional logic & branching 
• Human approval workflows 
• Notifications and automated follow-ups 
• Data extraction, transformation & validation 
• Basic Python 
• Testing, debugging and workflow troubleshooting 
   How I think about workflows: 
 TRIGGER → INPUT/VALIDATION → PROCESSING → AI DECISION → TOOLS/API CALLS → CONDITIONAL LOGIC → HUMAN APPROVAL → ACTION → CRM/DATABASE → NOTIFICATION → LOGGING → ERROR HANDLING 
 I’m not just interested in connecting random nodes together. I’m learning to think about the complete workflow, including what happens when APIs fail, data is missing, an AI response is incorrect, or a human needs to take over. 
   Projects I’ve personally built: 
   AI Lead Qualification System 
 • Lead enters through a form/webhook 
• AI analyzes and qualifies the lead 
• Structured result is generated 
• Result is stored in Google Sheets/CRM 
• Salesperson receives a notification 
   AI Local Prospecting Agent 
 • Takes a target location 
• Finds local businesses 
• Researches potential prospects 
• Qualifies whether they may need a service 
• Generates personalized outreach 
• Requires human approval before sending 
• Logs the results 
   AI Local Lead Hunter 
 I’m currently extending my prospecting system into a more complete lead-hunting workflow with research, qualification, personalization, approval and logging.(in progress) 
   AI Voice / Telephony 
 I have not yet built production systems with Retell, Vapi or Twilio, so I don’t want to pretend otherwise. 
 However, I understand the architecture behind these systems and how they connect with n8n, APIs, CRMs, calendars, lead qualification, notifications and human handoff. 
 I’m actively learning these areas and would be excited to work on them under real project requirements. 
   What I’m looking for: 
 • Remote freelance work 
• Part-time opportunities 
• Junior automation roles 
• Long-term agency collaboration 
• AI automation projects 
• Opportunities where I can contribute technically and keep improving 
 I’m especially interested in working with people who care about: 
 BUILD → TEST → DEPLOY → MONITOR → MAINTAIN 
 rather than simply making a workflow that works once. 
   What I can bring: 
 I’m comfortable learning unfamiliar APIs/tools, understanding an existing workflow, debugging problems, building from documentation, and improving workflows step by step. 
 I’m also happy to start with a  small technical task or demo  so you can see how I work before committing to anything larger. 
   If you’re building an AI automation agency, hiring an n8n developer, or need help building reliable n8n + AI workflows, feel free to comment or DM me. 
 I can share my projects, workflow screenshots, demos, and explain exactly what I personally built. 
 Looking forward to connecting with people building interesting things!

A few years ago, I had a series of health conditions that left me in unbearable suffering every moment of every day. At a certain point, when it was o
A few years ago, I had a series of health conditions that left me in unbearable suffering every moment of every day. At a certain point, when it was obvious that there was no probable way out, my mind reflexively starting tell me to kill myself. I would look at any menial object and my mind would automatically start considering ways I could use that object to end my life. This went on for months, on and off. I wouldn't say I "endured" it,  but I trained myself to just try to get through the next hour, or the next minute if things were really bad. I'm much better now and that experience in many ways helped me, but I have no romantic feelings about it and I'd prefer if it hadn't happened. If someone had given me a painless out that I could trust back then, I almost certainly would have taken it. Instead, I learned acceptance in a pretty awful way. I'm saying this for a specific reason: for many people, their suicide isn't some act of "giving up" or not being willing to endure;  it's that some physiological process has begun that strongly urges you to do it every moment of every day. I understand why people have some anger or disappointment with loved ones who have died by suicide, but I personally do not feel that way. After what I experienced, I'm just happy that any of us get a chance to live in peace at all.

source_text:
Show HN: PanelAlpha Engine – Turn your VPS into a programmable hosting layer
PanelAlpha Engine is an open-source hosting environment for your VPS, programmable through MCP, API and CLI. After ~2 years in the making (we started back in the non-ai era) we've decided to open source our Docker-based Engine. So far, we've used it as a back-end environment for WordPress sites and we have been distributing it through web hosting providers and larger agencies. It's been tested on a few thousand sites already. Now people are vibe coding, using AI for everything and building agentic workflows, while at the same time open source projects are getting through a reinassaince. So, not only we have open-sourced it ourselves, but we've also expanded it to support any web application and tested it against over a thousand repositories (and soon will be much more). You can use it with MCP, API or CLI to:
- deploy projects from files or git
- get a preview URL or use your own domain with automatic SSL
- restrict access with a password
- get built-in monitoring and visitor stats (no need for Google Analytics)
- manage databases, SFTP/FTP, CRON, firewall rules
- read through logs and debug
- create or restore backups (locally or remotely via S3/FTP)
- connect with Cloudflare (for tunnels and DNS)
... and much more (see docs). You install it with one command (you can also define a repo to be installed together with it) and then with another command connect your AI with it. Done. Your agent gets a hosting environment on your server without unrestricted root SSH access. You can even define its permissions. Our early users have asked us about the visual/panel - it will be available soon too (and also open source). Feel free to roast, we're open for feedback!

source_text:
Show HN: Ret – An inbox and canvas for your Codex and Claude Code agents
Over the last few weeks I've really been using Codex and Claude to solve a lot of parallel tasks, across a lot of different projects. This lead me to wishing that I could interface with my agents in the same way that I interface with my already existing windows and editors. For me, this usually means that I have like 5 to anywhere around 8 different windows that I drag around depending on where I want to focus, this could mean I am focusing on the terminal now, or I want to test stuff in a simulator or browser; but when I go to interface with agents, I have to manage many tabs, or I have to look through a list in their native apps. This is not convenient for me, and I'm almost certain this is not convenient for many of you. That's why I built an infinite canvas, where my traditional desktop style workflow can come to life alongside my agents, I can drag them around depending on where I want my focus to be, or I can let them just pile up, like the 15 finder windows you're hiding with your browser right now. But, when I do want to go back to that thread, I will intuitively just know right where it is. I didn't stop there though, I really enjoyed the inbox style agent interface that Google shipped many months ago with Anti Gravity, but I didn't really enjoy much other than that, so, I built that in too. But, I still didn't stop there, a traditional code editor still comes in handy every once and awhile, just to read, or to tradcode, though Ret doesn't feature a VS-Code fork, yet anyways, maybe one day something similar could exist, it does feature a fairly comparable implementation, powered by the same technology, in a similar layout, just without the plugins and bloat. But, I didn't stop there either, the traditional sidebar and one centered chat is a nice experience sometimes, so I built that in too. I guess you probably can see where this is going, but that's also not where I stopped. Working on a single focused thread can be beneficial, but I am a heavy fork user, so I made it convenient to work side by side your main thread and a fork, with ambitions to expand on this in the future as I feel out how many forks or side chats are worth working on at the same time in the 'focused' view. But focus view doesn't stop there, instead of having only one chat in focus, and having to then jump back to the sidebar, I thought, well hey, browser tabs are great, so I built those in too. I know it sounds like there's a lot of things built in  here, and there is, but trust me, it doesn't feel bloated at all, it feels amazing. I really think this is something that greatly benefits my productivity, and I hope that some of you also feel my excitement when trying it out.

> Not sure what to tell you. It's been a problem for decades and only gets worse It's been a problem for literally millennia. This hardly unique to 21
> Not sure what to tell you. It's been a problem for decades and only gets worse It's been a problem for literally millennia. This hardly unique to 21st century america. Yes, I'm glad you don't have a "problem child". That's genuinely great, I wish everyone was that lucky. What I would  like , in the smallest possible way, is some shred of empathy for people who aren't as lucky as you are. Perhaps you could practice the concept of "walking a mile in another man's shoes" and make an attempt to understand what they're dealing with instead of dismissing them as inferior. I'm also happy your wife is volunteering to help with girl scouts. I think that's a great thing and more people should do it. But that doesn't excuse your lack of empathy. Kids are not some kind of deterministic automatons where the same input always produces the same output (as if we could even reproduce the same inputs for an entire life). They're more complicated than that for reasons we frankly can't even understand. There are a number of things that are highly correlated with producing a "good child", a major one being having enough money that the family isn't under constant stress and you can afford second (or third or fourth) chances. But callously discarding every child who isn't lucky enough to benefit from this is just wrong. We, as a society, a culture, should be better than that. Am I expecting you, personally, to go out and change the world? No, no more than I'm expecting myself to do it. But we all make small decisions every day and if enough of us make the "right ones" they can add up, and it starts with empathy for our fellow man.

source_text:
C1 Backend — Role-Scoped Operational Work Queues & Query APIs
## Evidence

15 Oct repository audit found **no staff list/read APIs** for operations and Business Workspace reference screens are fixtures only. This is NEW BACKEND query capability; existing [GLO-83](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-83/build-hub-operations-console)/223/125 are UI projects, which remain paused.

## Implement ONLY NestJS owner-module API read contracts

* Admin: operational order attention queue, pending decisions, sourcing failures, fulfillment exceptions (small paginated/filterable summaries).
* Supplier: own consolidated PO inbox and line details with own confirmed/ready states; no PII or competitors' prices.
* Hub: assigned location receivable PO lines, per-Order preparation queue, ready shipments, optional assigned dispatch runs.
* Driver: own manifest/details including necessary secured pin/phone/COD and current status; reuse existing driver read API; no duplicate endpoint.
* Cashier/Admin: unsettled expected/declared collections + discrepancies, settlement history scoped to authorized hub.
* Support: case/exception actionable list if existing model permits; use canonical IDs, no independent state ownership.
* Use typed DTOs, bounded pagination, whitelisted sorting/filters, role+resource ownership checks, stable consistent statuses, no new denormalized parallel source of truth unless measured necessary.

## DoD

API documentation and role-by-role HTTP/DB tests show each actor sees its own work only; Driver B/Supplier B/Hub B denied cross-tenant/foreign records, PII minimized. No Next.js, dashboard layouts, auth UI, live SSE or generic reporting engine.

GMP Certification in Indonesia
GMP Certification in Indonesia – Good Manufacturing Practices
GMP Certification in Indonesia helps manufacturers establish controlled, hygienic, and consistent production practices that support product quality and safety. GMP, or Good Manufacturing Practices, provides principles for controlling manufacturing activities so products are produced and handled according to defined quality requirements.
GMP is particularly relevant to industries such as pharmaceuticals, food and beverages, cosmetics, medical devices, dietary supplements, and other sectors where manufacturing conditions can directly affect product safety and quality. Organizations can use GMP principles to strengthen production controls, documentation, hygiene, quality assurance, and traceability.
For professional guidance, explore[ GMP Certification in Indonesia](https://certvalue.com/gmp-certification-in-indonesia/).
What Is GMP Certification in Indonesia?
GMP Certification in Indonesia generally refers to an assessment, certification, inspection, or compliance process against applicable Good Manufacturing Practice requirements. The exact requirements depend on the product category, industry, applicable regulations, and relevant regulatory or certification scheme.
GMP focuses on controlling manufacturing risks throughout the product lifecycle. It can cover raw materials, personnel, facilities, equipment, production processes, quality control, sanitation, packaging, storage, documentation, and distribution.
Indonesian manufacturers may need to consider requirements established by relevant authorities, including the Indonesian Food and Drug Authority (BPOM), together with sector-specific regulations and customer requirements. Organizations should determine which GMP requirements and regulatory approvals apply to their specific products.
Why Is GMP Important for Indonesian Businesses?
Indonesia's manufacturing sector supplies products to both domestic and international markets. Maintaining consistent production conditions is essential for organizations whose products can affect consumer health, safety, or product performance.
GMP provides a systematic approach to identifying and controlling manufacturing risks. It encourages organizations to maintain suitable facilities, control raw materials, train employees, monitor processes, maintain equipment, and keep accurate production records.
Effective GMP practices can also support preparation for regulatory inspections, customer audits, supplier evaluations, and applicable market requirements. However, GMP certification or assessment does not automatically replace product registrations, licenses, approvals, or other legally required authorizations.
Benefits of GMP Certification in Indonesia
1. Consistent Product Quality
GMP controls help organizations standardize manufacturing activities and reduce variations that could affect product quality.
2. Improved Product Safety
Hygiene controls, sanitation procedures, equipment maintenance, and process monitoring can help reduce contamination and manufacturing-related risks.
3. Better Regulatory Preparedness
A structured GMP system can help organizations organize manufacturing activities around applicable regulatory and industry requirements.
4. Stronger Documentation and Traceability
Accurate production records, batch information, inspection results, and corrective action records help organizations track manufacturing activities and investigate quality issues.
5. Increased Customer Confidence
Documented manufacturing controls can provide customers, distributors, and business partners with greater confidence in an organization's production practices.
6. Reduced Operational Risks
Employee training, preventive maintenance, process controls, and defined procedures can reduce production errors, contamination risks, and inconsistent outputs.
Key Elements of GMP in Indonesia
An effective GMP framework commonly addresses:
Personnel: Appropriate training, hygiene, responsibilities, and competency.
Facilities: Suitable premises designed and maintained to support hygienic operations.
Equipment: Properly selected, cleaned, maintained, and controlled equipment.
Raw Materials: Controlled sourcing, inspection, identification, storage, and handling.
Production: Approved procedures and controlled manufacturing processes.
Quality Control: Appropriate inspection, testing, and product evaluation.
Documentation: Accurate procedures, production records, inspection records, and corrective actions.
Storage and Distribution: Controlled conditions that help preserve product quality.
GMP Certification Process in Indonesia
The process varies according to the industry, product, applicable regulations, and assessment arrangement.
Step 1: Initial Review
The organization identifies its products, manufacturing activities, applicable GMP requirements, and regulatory obligations.
Step 2: Gap Assessment
Facilities, processes, documentation, hygiene practices, equipment, and quality controls are reviewed to identify gaps.
Step 3: GMP System Development
Required procedures for production, sanitation, quality control, maintenance, training, documentation, and other activities are established or improved.
Step 4: Implementation and Training
Employees implement approved procedures and maintain appropriate records throughout manufacturing operations.
Step 5: Internal Evaluation
Internal audits, inspections, or management reviews may be conducted to identify weaknesses and corrective actions.
Step 6: Assessment and Corrective Action
The applicable inspection, assessment, certification, or regulatory process is completed and identified issues are addressed.
Step 7: Final Documentation
Certification, inspection records, regulatory documentation, or other evidence is issued according to the applicable scheme.
Why Choose CertValue for GMP Support in Indonesia?
CertValue provides consulting and certification-related support for organizations seeking to improve their manufacturing and compliance practices. Indonesian businesses can obtain guidance on GMP requirements, documentation, procedures, implementation, internal reviews, and assessment preparation.
The appropriate assessment depends on the product category, industry, applicable regulations, and selected certification or regulatory arrangement. Organizations should confirm whether they require certification, regulatory approval, inspection, registration, or another form of conformity documentation.
For more information, visit[ GMP Certification in Indonesia](https://certvalue.com/gmp-certification-in-indonesia/).
Conclusion
GMP Certification in Indonesia helps organizations establish controlled manufacturing practices focused on product quality, safety, consistency, hygiene, and traceability. By implementing appropriate procedures and maintaining effective production controls, businesses can strengthen their manufacturing operations and improve readiness for applicable regulatory and customer requirements.
Organizations seeking GMP implementation and certification-related support can contact CertValue for guidance on applicable requirements and available services.

Help Needed: Building an AI-Powered Personalized Fitness Plan Automation with n8n + Google Forms + WhatsApp
Hi everyone, 
 I’m currently working on an  AI-powered fitness automation using n8n , and I would appreciate some guidance from the community on how to design the workflow properly. 
 The basic idea is to create an automated system where a user first fills out a  Google Form  with their personal fitness requirements. The form would collect information such as: 
 
 
 Name 
 
 
 Age 
 
 
 Current weight 
 
 
 Target weight 
 
 
 Fitness goal 
 
 
 General fitness 
 
 
 Weight loss 
 
 
 Weight gain 
 
 
 Muscle building 
 
 
 Other goals 
 
 
 
 
 Current fitness level 
 
 
 Type of workout they prefer 
 
 
 Gym 
 
 
 Home workout 
 
 
 Outdoor workout 
 
 
 
 
 Available workout time 
 
 
 Dietary preferences 
 
 
 Food preferences/restrictions 
 
 
 Number of meals they prefer 
 
 
 Any relevant limitations or conditions they want the system to consider 
 
 
   Proposed n8n Workflow 
 I’m thinking of building something like: 
  Google Form → Google Sheets → n8n → AI → Personalized Fitness Plan → WhatsApp  
 After the user submits the form, n8n would collect and process the information and send it to an AI model. 
 The AI would then generate a  personalized daily fitness plan , including: 
    Workout Plan  
 
 
 Exercises for the day 
 
 
 Sets and repetitions 
 
 
 Workout duration 
 
 
 Rest periods 
 
 
 Gym/home workout variations 
 
 
    Daily Meal Plan  
 
 
 Breakfast 
 
 
 Lunch 
 
 
 Snacks 
 
 
 Dinner 
 
 
 Suggested food options 
 
 
 Approximate calorie and protein targets 
 
 
    Daily Targets  
 
 
 Estimated calorie target 
 
 
 Protein target 
 
 
 Water intake 
 
 
 Daily activity/step goal 
 
 
 Workout duration 
 
 
    Personalized Schedule  
The system should ideally generate a plan based on the user’s goal and preferences and provide a different daily plan as the user progresses. 
   WhatsApp Automation 
 Once the plan is generated, I want n8n to automatically send it to the user through  WhatsApp . 
 For example: 
 
  Good Morning, Rahul!    
   Goal: Weight Loss 
  Today’s Target: ~2,000 kcal 
  Water: 2.5–3 L 
    Today’s Workout  
• Squats – 3 × 12 
• Push-ups – 3 × 10 
• Walking – 30 min 
    Breakfast  
• Eggs + oats + fruit 
    Lunch  
• Rice/roti + vegetables + protein source 
    Dinner  
• … 
 Have a great workout!   
 
 I would also like to eventually add  daily reminders , progress tracking, and possibly allow users to update their weight or progress through WhatsApp. 
   What I Need Help With 
 I would especially appreciate suggestions on: 
 
 
  How should I structure the n8n workflow?  
 
 
 Which nodes would be best for processing the Google Form/Google Sheets data? 
 
 
 What is the best way to structure the  AI prompt  so that the generated plans are consistent and personalized? 
 
 
 How should I maintain a user’s information and progress over multiple days? 
 
 
 What is the best approach for sending the generated plan through  WhatsApp ? 
 
 
 How can I create a system where the AI generates a new plan each day rather than repeating the same plan?

# TYME-HALL-LAUNCH-001 — Independent Reviewer and Release Steward Qualification

**Priority:** P0 · **State:** OPEN / UNASSIGNED / NO ACCESS GRANTED · **Release target:** October 30, 2026 (conditional)  
**Governing command:** [Notion launch command](https://app.notion.com/p/3f5c51d54b758197a92ff59d2c203045) · [Launch dependency ledger #15](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-control-center/issues/15)  
**Authority posture:** human-governed. No issue, model or agent may grant GitHub merge/release privileges, production publication, payment, secrets, contributor identity, or Canon promotion.

## Why this gate is P0

Current [Hall ruleset #24880323](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/rules/24880323) is active and requires **one approving review**, last-push approval, stale approval dismissal, resolved conversations, and no bypass. Independent GitHub review is currently missing for:
- [Hall PR #19](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/pull/19) — Office freshness and premerge checks (draft).
- [Hall PR #20](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/pull/20) — controlled production release (draft; 38 offline test cases passed, not a live deploy).
- [Control Center PR #18](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-control-center/pull/18) — release packet/assurance evidence (draft).

**Production safety constraint:** Authenticated Cloudflare Pages `codex-interface` still has Git-triggered automatic **production** deploys enabled on `main`, while all preview deployments remain enabled. The production-only auto-build freeze must be **separately authorized and verified OFF BEFORE merging either Hall PR**; a code-only merge could otherwise publish without a separate founder release GO. Live Cloudflare settings, main, ruleset, secrets and GitHub environments are unchanged by this issue.

## Separated human responsibilities (do not collapse)

| Role | Mandate | Authority NOT conferred |
|---|---|---|
| A — independent code reviewer | Review exact PR head, changed files, denials, test evidence, supply chain, route preservation, licensing/privacy and rollback; return an independently attributable review | Not authorized to publish, modify Cloudflare, change GitHub rulesets, grant credentials, spend funds, approve Canon or sign founder GO |
| B — production release operator | When qualified and designated, manually start a release workflow against a specific independently reviewed `main` SHA | Cannot independently approve their own environment execution or expand release scope |
| C — founder / delegated separate human release approver | Record a distinct, explicit G6 GO and approve the protected deployment environment for an exact source SHA after all release gates pass | No hidden model/agent delegation; does not waive independent technical review |

Role B and role C **must be different human actors** when environment self-review prevention applies. Technical independence requires reviewer A not to be the author of the reviewed change. A public participant completing a cold-read/a11y test under [Hall issue #18](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/issues/18) is not thereby qualified to approve security-sensitive source code or obtain write access.

## Qualification protocol — evidence before access

- [ ] **Q1 — public-only screening:** Verify candidate controls the claimed GitHub identity. Request an uncoached review of these public artifacts, without credentials, private links, tokens or remote machine access. Record disclosure of affiliations/conflicts and scope availability.
- [ ] **Q2 — exercise technical judgment:** Require concrete file/line findings for at least one release-blocking case (e.g. production autobuild before merge; environment declaration without required reviewer; wrong/moved SHA; false route equivalence; supply-chain version pinning; bypass; credentials exposure) and a safe reproducible verification approach. Distinguish observed defects from speculation.
- [ ] **Q3 — understand governance:** Candidate must explicitly acknowledge GitHub review != founder G6, green CI != live Cloudflare deployment, test receipts != institutionally durable positive Phase 2, and new participants receive no implied identity/governance rights.
- [ ] **Q4 — identify least privilege:** Confirm GitHub's minimum permissions for an eligible required PR review under current repository rules and plan, separately from a mere commenter. Obtain explicit founder authorization **before** adding collaborator access. No Admin, Cloudflare, repo secrets, bypass actors, environment approver, or unattended automation credentials in initial reviewer assignment.
- [ ] **Q5 — source/head-specific review:** Obtain review of PR #19 and PR #20 against current head SHAs, explicit unresolved findings and one approving review only after defects have been addressed. Existing ruleset must never be bypassed. Review Control Center PR #18 independently if qualification extends to governance packet review.
- [ ] **Q6 — release operator vs founder:** Designate named human release operator and a separate founder-controlled environment reviewer; manually inspect actual `tymehall-production` required-reviewer settings, protected-main branch restriction, no-bypass/self-review posture, and protected environment-only secrets. **Do not rely on the YAML environment field alone**.
- [ ] **Q7 — staging/denial evidence:** Verify manual release source SHA equality, controlled asset route diff, missing-credential denial, unapproved environment denial, branch-race denial, isolated staging run, rollback and independent production readback. No live mutation before separate explicit authorization.
- [ ] **Q8 — documented acceptance:** Record actual reviewer GitHub login, scope of review, timestamp, exact PR commit SHAs, linked test evidence, outstanding findings, permissible permissions, independent founder authority, and GO/HOLD decision. If no qualified reviewer, retain intentional freeze.

## Public invitation posture

**Do not offer a paid bounty yet.** The related mobile cold-read contribution candidate is [UNFUNDED](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/issues/18). If recruiting volunteers, begin with a bounded public documentation/code-review exercise using only published material. No promised compensation, privilege, institutional authority or project endorsement. Screen attempts to redirect toward wallets, off-platform payment, unverifiable automated test claims or demands for credentials. Keep original issue #18's spam lock intact.

source_text:
Has anyone built a reliable multichannel inventory system that actually keeps up during flash sales?
Running into a wall that I suspect a lot of sellers here have hit. 
 We’re selling across Shopify and two marketplaces. Everything runs fine during normal trading. The moment we run any kind of promotional event flash sale, limited drop, festive season push inventory starts drifting across channels. 
 A sale happens on one platform and by the time the other channels update, we’ve already taken orders we can’t fulfil. It’s not a huge volume problem - it’s a timing problem. The sync just isn’t fast enough when orders are coming in quickly from multiple places simultaneously. 
 We’ve tried a few apps from the App Store but most of them seem to operate on a scheduled sync every 10, 15 or 30 minutes. Which is fine at low volume but completely breaks down the moment anything sells quickly. 
 What I think we actually need is something event-driven, where a sale on any channel immediately triggers an update everywhere else, rather than waiting for the next scheduled job to run. 
 Has anyone solved this properly? Specifically looking for: 
 -> Real-time sync across Shopify and external marketplaces → Somthing that handles concurrent orders without overselling → Ideally a single dashboard for orders across all channels too 
 Would genuinely love to know what’s working for people here whether that’s an App Store solution, a custom setup or something else entirely.

I think a lot of us are trying really hard here to avoid the simplest and most obvious answer, which is that AI coding software is helpful, but doesn'
I think a lot of us are trying really hard here to avoid the simplest and most obvious answer, which is that AI coding software is helpful, but doesn't deliver the kind of productivity gains boosters are talking about. There's a bunch of reasons for this, but the obvious one to me is just that I haven't seen  any  backed up claims that actually break down how a 10x (or similar) speed up would get delivered in practice. For the sake of an example, let's imagine an engineer who works an 8 hour day split up like this: - 2 hours: investigating and debugging potential issues - 1 hour: reviewing code - 2 hours: in various team meetings, catch ups or otherwise - 1 hour: designing (including at a level of writing code for prototyping etc) - 2 hours: actually writing code I think that's a semi-reasonable day breakdown. Realistically, I think AI helps debug faster, and generate code faster. Possibly design work too, but I think this isn't really the case since AI workflows necessitate a lot  more  design work in order to make the AI generation deterministic. So looking at that day, if I was able to fully automate writing code  and  debugging issues so that it took 0 time at all (which I think is a very optimistic assessment of the actual speed ups AI provides), we're looking at a 2x speed up of an engineers productivity. If we think AI makes those things twice as fast (so 2 hours, instead of 4) the engineer is now at a 1.25x speed up. That's great, but it's hardly revolutionary. It'll change your output something like the way going from a team of 4 to a team of 5 might do. This is obviously complete conjecture and I'm sure the average time engineers spend on things is different, but I think there's an obvious take away. If you want to make claims about the performance impact of code, you need to know  where the code spends its time , and  what impact you're making on those sections of code . Similarly, if you want to know what performance gains are being made, you need to know  what engineers spend their time doing  and  what impact AI is having of those tasks . I've seen very little attempt to actually make realistic claims on that basis, and a lot of vibes-based "wooah, AI makes me so much faster" type claims. Those claims are obviously not nothing, but I wouldn't trust people's gut reactions to make serious claims about the overall productivity changes in our entire industry.

source_text:
Show HN: Atticus – Hold-to-talk voice assistant for macOS that runs on Claude -p
Hi HN! I'm Saarth. I'm in 9th grade, and I built Atticus. Atticus is a fast and cheap Mac assistant that can do tasks for you. You hold down Control-Option-Space, speak or type your task, be it complex or a simple browser search, and Atticus will get on it. The interesting part is that simple tasks, like opening apps, playing a Spotify playlist, or web queries, don't touch AI, and instead are processed locally and typically finish in under a second. For example, prompting Atticus to open apps takes around 0.08 seconds, sometimes even finishing before you finish your sentence, sort of like Jev. Any tasks that are more complicated will be sent to Claude via claude -p, meaning you never need an API key and Atticus will run on your existing Claude Pro or Max plan. By using this approach, costs are also cut down immensely, with, on average, tasks costing a fraction of a cent. To achieve Atticus' speed, it remembers shortcuts from each task it completes. When it does a task right for the first time, it saves its steps and replays them the next time without AI. For example, a workflow of creating a new meeting took about 30 seconds the first time around. Atticus then logs the exact steps to memory and takes 5-8 seconds on the next pass. To add to this, Atticus also learns about you as you use it more and from what's on your computer, including your name, your apps, and things you want it to remember, personalizing its answers to you. To combat the safety concerns over giving an AI unrestricted access to your device, Atticus has toggleable restrictions, so before anything is deleted, sent, bought, or written to a file, the user is prompted before that action. Some features I'm currently working on include a meeting copilot that capitalizes on Atticus' speed, allowing Atticus to listen in on meetings and answer questions in real time as they come in, personalized to the context of the meeting and what it knows about you. To run Atticus, macOS 26 or higher is required for its voice transcription features. The voice transcription is also done locally by macOS. Atticus is free, open source, and also very fresh, and I'm completely aware of its many rough edges, which is why I'd love to hear from everyone about what breaks and what you guys would like to see Atticus do!

China Industrial Electronics Sourcing 
I need an experienced, on-the-ground China-based sourcing agent to secure reliable industrial-grade electronics for my production line—specifically PCBs, electronic modules, and any closely related components that fall under the industrial electronics umbrella  ( TPU injection molding manufacturers , gateway components, SS inserts  ) .  The process will start with samples for field testing in my country, followed by purchases that will gradually increase in volume.

Your role starts at supplier identification and finishes only once the goods are on a carrier, export-ready. I expect you to:  

• Build a short-list of vetted factories or distributors able to meet industrial specifications and international certifications  
• Negotiate pricing, minimum order quantities, lead times, payment terms, and sample availability  
• Perform physical or third-party quality inspections on PCBs and modules before shipment  
• Consolidate orders if multiple items are involved and arrange cost-effective logistics to my freight forwarder  

To streamline communication, please be comfortable working with English documentation, provide photo/video evidence of factory visits when possible, and keep all quotes in RMB and USD. Experience around Shenzhen, Dongguan, or other electronics hubs is a plus, and fluency with platforms such as Alibaba, 1688, or made-to-order contract manufacturers will help you move quickly.

Acceptance criteria 
1. Supplier report (Excel or Google Sheet) listing at least three verified sources per item, including contact info, quoted price, lead time, and certification status  
2. Signed pro-forma invoice from selected supplier(s) reflecting the negotiated terms  
3. Inspection report with photos/videos confirming quality before goods leave the factory  
4. Tracking or booking confirmation from the chosen logistics provider  

If this scope fits your expertise, pls get in touch
Budget: $250-750 USD

source_text:
Human approval in n8n: what does the reviewer actually need to see?
Hello everyone, 
 I’m one of the creators of Ratifia, a play on “ratify.” We build 
human-in-the-loop tooling for approvals in automated workflows that are auditable and reliable. 
 The question I keep coming back to is whether the person receiving an approval 
request has enough to actually decide. Not whether the workflow paused 
correctly, but whether the human on the other end understood what they were 
being asked to approve and what would happen when they said yes. 
 The problem that led us here is that adding an approval step is usually 
straightforward. Making it work for the people involved is the hard part: 
getting the right context in front of the right person, handling the wait, and 
being able to say afterward what was approved and what actually happened. 
 Our existing design partners have shaped a lot of the product, and most of what 
they changed was on the human side of it: what the reviewer sees, how much 
context is too much, and what they need to know about where a value came from. 
Now I’d like to learn from different industries, different workflows, and 
different ideas about where the human belongs. 
 I know n8n has human review for tool calls, and for plenty of cases that is 
enough. Where we spend our time is the narrower question of keeping the action 
that runs tied to the approval that was given, and preserving the evidence 
you’ll need a month later. 
 Our view is that this isn’t purely a tooling problem. It takes good workflow 
patterns and software that makes those patterns practical. We want to develop 
both alongside people dealing with these problems in real projects. 
 That’s why I’m posting instead of building another feature. I’m looking for two 
or three people running production workflows with consequential or 
hard-to-reverse actions: refunds, customer emails, sensitive record changes, or 
money movement. 
 Being a design partner means we work directly with you on the integration rather 
than pointing you at docs. We start by recording which actions would have 
required approval, before anything blocks, so you see what it would do before 
you turn on enforcement. 
 In return, I’m looking for a real workflow and honest feedback, including “this 
is wrong.” We’ll learn the most from workflows where a mistaken action has a 
real consequence and someone is responsible for the outcome. 
 If that sounds like your setup, I’d like to hear what you’re building and where 
your current approach falls short. Reply here or DM me. You can also take a look 
at  ratifia.com . 
 P.S. 
The node lands on npm this week. Self-hosted, you install it from Settings, 
Community nodes. On Cloud you can run the same thing with HTTP Request nodes 
today.

source_text:
Show HN: shadowclone, skills learned from your coding agent corrections
shadowclone reads the coding-agent sessions already on your disk, finds where you corrected the agent and turns those corrections into skills your agents load next time. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and Antigravity. Every capture source is off by default and has its own consent setting. Why I'm building it? I use multiple harnesses and agents, I extensively use Claud Code and Codex, but I also use Cursor and Antigravity every now and then. I didn't want to have to teach every harness or model the things I taught the other ones between my last session and the current one. I also cannot have my personal rules and preferences in all the repositories I work on because my collaborators may have varying levels of trust with AI and their own preferences. shadowclone helps me build and improve trust with my agents so I can give them more autonomy while running multiple sessions in parallel. --- Who is this for? If you only use Claude or Codex or any one of these, you may not need the shadowclone CLI and the harness and agent you use might already be sufficient. But, if you are like me and work across harnesses and agents, shadowclone will help you avoid repeating your preferences each time. --- Built-in skills and skill builds shadowclone is also great for someone who is just now adopting AI into their coding workflows because it ships with several skills that they can use to customize their agent's behavior. They can equip all the skills, or just some of them, they'll see the "personality" their agent gets from equipping those skills from the `shadowclone wizard`. --- Setup is extremely easy, just ask your Claude Code, or Codex, or another agent - "Set up shadowclone:  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/mai... " --- Privacy shadowclone is free and open source, it uses the MIT license. It doesn't have a subscription, or a server. It just uses your existing agent subscription i.e. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or even your local model via Pi. You can explicitly disable sources, it also redacts any and all sensitive information it uses for learning. --- PR reviews and Cloud bots It can review PRs with the `shadowclone review` command, it ships a guided review skill that will perform a deep review of your code (or someone else's) and produce an HTML document you can annotate, add comments to and submit so your agent can stage a draft review on the PR you are reviewing. --- Evals I performed several evals, I won't describe them here, all of them are available in the repository -  https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main/evals  --- Comparison to other tools? You can also see how it compares to other tools here -  https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main#how-shad...

[C2] Firmware and final assembly outputs remain outside this review
Review finding **C2** — firmware and final assembly confirmation for bonanzaDisplay v3.1.

**Current status:** Local fabrication/assembly review package regenerated from pushed commit `0fab1cac237adbfad9c7c31abaaa868e837f4df0`, including the approved R12 substitution to C270615. ERC, DRC, schematic parity and manufacturing preflight pass. Only R12 part metadata changed; connectivity and geometry are unchanged. The package is **for upload review, not approved for ordering**. Firmware source and assembled-hardware test evidence have not been supplied; JLCPCB's actual preview has not been viewed.

**Local package:** `Manufacturing Files/bonanzaDisplay-v3.1-r12-review/` (ignored local outputs).

- `Gerbers-JLCPCB.zip`: six copper layers, both mask/silk/paste layers, outline, separate PTH/NPTH drills and Gerber job.
- `BOM-JLCPCB.csv`: 27 exact LCSC selections, 52 fitted components.
- `CPL-JLCPCB.csv`: exactly the same 52 references, all Bottom. Excludes J2/J15, 11 test pads and four fiducials. Retains SW3 despite its through-hole footprint attribute. USB remains fitted as in the current design.
- `placement-audit.csv`, `source-metadata-review.csv`, `parts-review.csv`, `excluded-components.csv`, source/output hash manifest, schematic/assembly PDFs and visual-review images.
- `RELEASE-REVIEW.md` and `firmware-checklist.md` document the remaining checks.

**Placement conventions:** Gerber/drill/CPL share the absolute origin. CPL uses positive X right and positive Y up. Existing Fabrication Toolkit manual offsets and bottom-side rotation conversion are applied, with auto-translate off. Native KiCad pad bounds are used for J6/SW3 center-origin placement. Existing corrections still require supplier model verification.

**Firmware requirements confirmed from schematic:** BS1=1 / BS0=0 selects 8-bit 8080 parallel. D0–D7=GPIO0–7, RES=GPIO8, CS=GPIO9, DC=GPIO10, WR=GPIO11, RD=GPIO12. Encoder B/CW=GPIO13, push=GPIO14, A/CCW=GPIO15, common=GND; pullups/debounce must be enabled in firmware. OLED internal VDD-regulator/reset and external VSL configuration must match the fitted module. Hardware testing must cover crystal/USB startup, ROM BOOT and display/encoder operation. H4 power sequencing remains explicitly deferred under #7.

**Completion criteria:**

- [x] Generate a local BOM/CPL review package with deliberate exclusions and matching reference sets.
- [x] Apply and audit existing placement offsets and coordinate conventions.
- [x] Run local checks and visually review generated Gerbers and native board rendering.
- [ ] Reconcile remaining source metadata and approve supplier pickup/rotation mapping (#13).
- [x] Apply the stocked R12 alternative (#10): C270615 / 0402WGF3092TCE; live stock 83,348 when checked. Confirm quantity/reservation in the actual order.
- [ ] Validate firmware implementation against display and encoder requirements.
- [ ] Validate crystal/USB/BOOT/display behavior on assembled hardware over intended conditions.
- [ ] Confirm actual six-layer filled-and-capped via order options and supplier stencil/CAM review (#12).
- [ ] Review and approve JLCPCB component matches, rotations, polarity and pickup offsets before ordering.

**Evidence:** `review/c2-release/` contains export script/command log, native IPC snapshots, catalog responses and checks. Sources: [EA OLED datasheet](https://www.lcd-module.de/fileadmin/html-seiten/eng/pdf/grafik/W256064-XALG.pdf), [JLCPCB BOM/CPL guidance](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/advice-for-bom-and-cpl-files-preparation), [Fabrication Toolkit conversion implementation](https://github.com/bennymeg/Fabrication-Toolkit/blob/7f627b6be76081b962161b9eb9fe3a326a18c915/plugins/process.py).

source_text:
MCP Server Trigger v2: tools/call right after session re-initialize succeeds but response is never delivered (hangs until 524) 
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

Describe the problem/error/question

MCP Server Trigger (v2): a tools/call sent right after a session re-initialize runs successfully, but its response is never delivered, so the request hangs until Cloudflare returns 524.

When an MCP session expires, n8n answers the next tools/call with 404 (session not found). The client (Claude Code, using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, streamable HTTP) then sends initialize and notifications/initialized and immediately re-sends the same tools/call. n8n runs the tool and it succeeds in 2–5 s, but no response headers are ever written to that POST. The request hangs until n8n Cloud's Cloudflare front end returns 524. The execution stays open about 125 s and is recorded with status success at the moment the connection drops.

This happened on 9 of 17 session-expiry retries over five days (2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09). It never happened on any other tool call: 0 of the other 226 tool executions on the same workflow.

Request sequence (one representative case; all nine match):

t (UTC) | Request | Response -- | -- | -- 14:20:37.9 | POST tools/call (old session id) | 404 session not found 14:20:38.6 | POST initialize | 200, new mcp-session-id 14:20:39.0 | POST notifications/initialized | 202 14:20:39.2 | POST notifications/initialized (client sends it twice) | 202 ~14:20:39 | POST tools/call (same tool, new session id) | nothing until 14:22:44.6, then 524 14:20:41.4 | POST tools/list | 200 14:20:48.2 | POST tools/call (same tool, same new session, client sends it again) | 200 in ~2 s

Expected: a tools/call on a freshly initialized session returns its JSON-RPC result, as a JSON body or an SSE event on the POST, as soon as the tool finishes. That is what happens for every other call, including the client's own second attempt a few seconds later on the same session.

Actual: the tool runs and succeeds, but the result never reaches the POST that asked for it. The request gets no response headers at all, and the execution stays open until the connection is cut.

What we have not established: the hung call arrives within ~0.5 s of initialize, alongside the notifications/initialized posts and before tools/list. The 8 retries that succeeded were sent slightly later. A race between session setup and the first request on the new session would fit this (for example, the response being written to a transport other than the one the POST is waiting on), but we have not confirmed it.

Our workaround: the proxy in front of n8n now answers any POST that has no response headers after 30 s with a retryable error, so the client re-sends instead of waiting for the 524.

Reproduction outline (not yet tried in isolation):

  1. MCP Server Trigger v2 with any fast tool attached, published.

  2. Open a streamable-HTTP MCP session, then let it expire so the next tools/call gets 404.

  3. Immediately initialize a new session, send notifications/initialized, and without waiting for tools/list send the tools/call again.

  4. The tool node runs and succeeds in the execution log, but the POST never receives response headers.

What is the error message (if any)?

No n8n error. The execution is marked success. The client receives HTTP 524 from Cloudflare after ~100 s with no response headers from n8n.

Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording

The workflow is one MCP Server Trigger (@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.mcpTrigger, typeVersion 2, streamable HTTP, header authentication) with read-only tools attached: httpRequestTool (typeVersion 4.4) and built-in app tool nodes. Every tool returns in seconds. The workflow JSON contains internal endpoints, so we have not pasted it here. We can share it, with execution ids and exact timestamps, privately with the n8n team.

The client reaches the trigger through a stateless reverse proxy, one replica, that forwards mcp-session-id, mcp-protocol-version, content-type, accept and last-event-id unchanged, so requests arrive in the order the client sends them.

Share the output returned by the last node

For the hung call in the table above, the execution shows:

  • Tool node: startTime 14:20:39, executionTime 1,926 ms, executionStatus success, about 18 KB of output.

  • MCP Server Trigger node: run recorded at 14:22:44 (0 ms). The execution's startedAt/stoppedAt are 14:22:44.69 / 14:22:44.72, so it was recorded only when the connection closed, about 125 s after the tool finished.

Across all nine hung calls: tool runtime 1.9–5.0 s (all success), tool start to execution close 125 s every time, response size 7–64 KB. Every other tool execution in the period closed within ~2 s of its tool finishing; the slowest tool runtime of all 235 was 11.9 s.

Ask HN: Fake abuse reports keep auto-blocking my site on Cloudflare
I run a small site on Cloudflare's Pro plan. Since 26 September, someone has filed the same fake abuse report against it six times. Each time, Cloudflare automatically puts a "Suspected Malware" warning on my homepage and login pages, and it stays until a person reviews it. The reports are word for word identical. They describe an "order" and product pages that have never existed on my site (they return 404). The file hash in the report doesn't match the hash in its own VirusTotal link, which returns "Item not found". Only the date changes, and twice it's been misspelled ("October 52026", "Octoboer 8 2026"). Cloudflare's team has cleared four of them. The reporter pastes the same text again within a day. The result is that my homepage has been blocked for most of two weeks, my traffic has halved, and Google is indexing the warning page instead of my site. I've opened support cases and requested reviews each time. I've had one reply, on 5 October, and nothing on a lasting fix. I'm not asking for special treatment. I'd like to know:
1. Is there a way to stop automatic mitigations from a reporter or text that has already been shown to be false?
2. Is there a manual-review setting for a domain?
3. Has anyone else seen the abuse form used like this, and how did it end? The same problem is described in my open case with Cloudflare (#02370521). Thanks for any pointers, and if anyone from Cloudflare's abuse team reads this, I'd welcome a reply.

> for both a format and secure protocol No, there is a working draft of a protocol. The "format" is only for use in the protocol, not a separate thing
> for both a format and secure protocol No, there is a working draft of a protocol. The "format" is only for use in the protocol, not a separate thing. Thus, giving the user a file is disallowed under the spec as per §5.1.1.1 which reads     > Explicitly state that the orchestrating party only transmits the credential exchange data between the exporting provider and importing provider.
  
And, in accordance with the spec, 1Password refuses to export passkeys directly to users for manual import on another platform or app. FIDO developers have complained about Keepassxc violating the spec and threatened to blacklist them as a result[1]. Furthermore, 1Password (who is apparently leading the way on the FIDO exchange protocol design) has not implemented _any_ passkey export on _any_ desktop platform. It is interesting that you listed Bitwarden, since I believe that FIDO developers have specifically disavowed Bitwarden's behavior of allowing users to access their passkeys. source_text:
Question: would an AEAP-shaped Execution Receipt fit the approval boundary already in procure-agent?

你好 刘正享,

I came across procure-agent via GitHub search for LangGraph + human-approval workflows and read through the README carefully. The combination of a LangGraph StateGraph with explicit interrupt points, SQLite checkpointer, Decimal-deterministic money arithmetic, and the explicit "approval has checkpoint-version verification; does not execute email or procurement transactions" boundary is unusually careful work. The `BOUNDARY_TEST_RESULTS.json` file in the repo suggests you've already thought about this surface.

My team at Aiyoplane published the first public draft of **AEAP** (Aiyo Execution Authorization Protocol) earlier this month. It overlaps with your approval boundary in a specific, narrow way, so I thought I'd ask rather than guess whether it fits.

**The overlap:**

Your current approval design verifies the LangGraph checkpoint version before an approval can resume execution. AEAP goes one step further: it produces a cryptographically-signed **Execution Receipt** (Ed25519 over an RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized intent) that binds the approver's identity to the exact tool invocation and arguments at the moment of approval. If the plan state changes between approval and execution — even in ways the checkpoint version doesn't detect — the receipt no longer validates and the tool fails closed.

For procure-agent's shape, that would mean: when a human approves a specific quote (报价 A at 1195.00 CNY from a specific supplier), the receipt binds that exact quote-ID + supplier + amount. A later resumed run cannot silently execute against a different quote, even if the LangGraph state looks consistent.

We shipped `aiyoplane-langgraph` and `aiyoplane-langchain` (both Python, Apache 2.0, zero credentials to run locally). Rough shape of what it would look like on your `evaluate_plan` tool:

```python
from aiyoplane_langchain import create_aiyo_langchain, create_local_rdp, BlockedByPolicy, EscalationRequired

authz = create_aiyo_langchain(
    rdp=create_local_rdp(policy=load_policy("procure-policy.yaml")),
    tool_config={
        "evaluate_plan": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "finish_sourcing": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "search_suppliers": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "request_quote": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "inspect_offer": {"aiyo_gated": False},
    },
)

@authz.wrap("evaluate_plan")
def evaluate_plan(args, ctx):
    # Runs only on ALLOW. ctx.receipt binds the approver + quote + supplier.
    # ESCALATE → EscalationRequired (fits your LangGraph interrupt pattern).
    # BLOCK   → BlockedByPolicy  (fits your "报告本轮未找到可执行方案" rule).
    return commit_procurement_plan(args)
```

**Three specific questions, since you'd know best:**

1. Is the approval boundary in procure-agent intentionally scoped to checkpoint-version verification only (meaning signed receipts would be out of scope on purpose), or is it a layer you'd consider adding?
2. If it's a layer you'd consider: would the fit be at `evaluate_plan` / `finish_sourcing` (where the plan commits) or at `request_quote` (where each quote is pulled)?
3. For the real-model mode where `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is live, is the "model cannot overwrite the hard rules" invariant something you'd want cryptographically enforced, or is the tool-side forced verification already sufficient for your use case?

If AEAP doesn't fit procure-agent's shape, closing this issue is a perfectly good answer — I'd rather hear "not a fit" than have you consider something that doesn't match.

Spec: [github.com/aiyoplane/aeap](https://github.com/aiyoplane/aeap) · aiyoplane-langchain: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain/) · aiyoplane-langgraph: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph/) · Trust surface, including §15 non-guarantees: [aiyoplane.com/trust](https://aiyoplane.com/trust)

Thanks for the careful work on this surface. The combination of Decimal arithmetic, explicit boundary tests, and the "不执行邮件或采购交易" ("does not execute email or procurement transactions") constraint is a pattern worth more of in agent projects.

— Rashon

source_text:
Show HN: Chkit – Schema, migrations and backfills for ClickHouse (like Drizzle)
Hey HN, im Marc, co-founder of ObsessionDB.
We are open sourcing ChKit, our tooling to manage schemas, migrations and backfills for clickhouse. I am a big fan of the type safety drizzle provides for the database. Manage the schema in typescript and generate migrations from it is a powerful workflow. I always wished something like it would exist for clickhouse, so we could manage our analytical workloads the same way. It didn't exist, so we build it. We build it after running ClickHouse at petabyte scale in our previous company, were we managed hundreds of tables, MVs and endpoints reading from them. The way it works: 1. You define your schema in typescript, with typed helpers for tables, mv, column types etc..
2. You generate the migration, that contains the DDL, to get your clickhouse instance from status quo to what your current typescript schema defines
3. Your CI can check for drift
4. You run the generated migration against production
5. You use the defined types in your code, to ingest your data while making sure it has the correct type.
   Bonus: if your schema change was BC breaking, we generate the sequence on how to backfill the data, into the intermediate table to migrate (this is quite the hard problem with large tables and schema evolution) In case you have already a clickhouse instance with a schema, you can pull it down and start using ChKit from where you are. Run our generator to setup the boilerplate:     npm create chkit@latest
  
If you folks are running clickhouse in production, I am curious to hear what other challenges you are running into.

source_text:
Microsoft Teams Trigger silently stops receiving messages after ~3 days (Graph subscription is never renewed)
### Bug Description

The **Microsoft Teams Trigger** (channel messages) creates a Microsoft Graph change-notification subscription when the workflow is published/activated, but nothing ever renews it. Graph caps `channelMessage` subscriptions at 4320 minutes (3 days), so the trigger stops receiving messages roughly 3 days after each activation or n8n restart. The workflow still shows as **Active**, no execution fails and no error is raised: the trigger is simply silent. In our case it went unnoticed for 12 days (messages with photos were not processed).

What we observed (delegated OAuth credential `microsoftTeamsOAuth2Api`; first seen on 2.39.10, same node code on 2.42.6):

1. After re-publishing the workflow, `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` listed one subscription for `/teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages` with `expirationDateTime` exactly 72 h after creation (2026-10-09T17:13:25Z -> 2026-10-12T17:13:25Z). It was unchanged 3 days later, i.e. no renewal happened.
2. Graph lifecycle notifications (`@odata.type: "#microsoft.graph.subscription"`, only the subscription id present) are delivered to the workflow as normal trigger items shortly before expiry. Nothing handles them (no PATCH, no re-authorize, no re-create); users have to filter them out manually.
3. From reading `MicrosoftTeamsTrigger.node.ts`: `checkExists()` only lists subscriptions and keeps those valid for more than 5 minutes; `create()` creates them and `delete()` removes them. We could not find renewal logic or handling of `reauthorizationRequired` / `subscriptionRemoved`.

Related (not GitHub issues): https://community.n8n.io/t/problem-teams-trigger-webhook/147354 (users report the same ~3 day expiry; workarounds: nightly PATCH or nightly unpublish/publish).

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with **Microsoft Teams Trigger** on a channel (resource: channel message) using a delegated OAuth credential.
2. Publish it and post a message in the channel: the workflow executes.
3. Wait more than 72 hours without republishing the workflow or restarting n8n.
4. Post a message in the channel: no execution is created. `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/subscriptions` no longer lists a valid subscription for the channel.
5. Unpublish + publish again: it works for another ~3 days.

### Expected behavior

The trigger keeps working indefinitely while the workflow is active, as Microsoft requires apps to renew subscriptions before expiry (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/subscription). Either renew the subscription periodically (`PATCH /subscriptions/{id}` with a new `expirationDateTime`, which also re-authorizes it), and/or handle the lifecycle notifications Graph sends (`reauthorizationRequired` -> PATCH; `subscriptionRemoved` -> re-create) instead of passing them to the workflow as items. At the very least, failing to keep the subscription alive should be visible (workflow status, execution error or log), since today the workflow looks healthy while it receives nothing.

Workaround we use: a separate scheduled workflow (twice a day) that does `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` with the same credential, picks the subscription whose `resource` matches the channel, and `PATCH`es its `expirationDateTime` to now + 4300 min; it alerts if none exists or the PATCH fails.

Ask HN: Are there AI models for generating sounds based on a text and reference?
I've been having a hard time finding a solution. Is there really no commercialized model that I can feed in a reference sound and text instruction and get another sound out? Right now having a multimodal inputs to image or text output is a commodotized, solved problem. IE you can put a prompt for some image and use a reference image to guide the model on what you want. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words right? Ive also used a text and audio input in order to get a text description or classification out. I cannot for the life of me find a solution for Audio + text -> Audio My usecase is that I'm trying to generate new sound effects based on a source that doesn't have that many clean examples and thought this would be just another solved workflow but I'm not finding much. Tried elevenlabs SFX but it's only text->audio and without the reference, it's hard to guide with just text and recreate a sound with any accuracy. I tried the Stable Audio 3 model which is supposed to do what I want but the results were terrible. This modality seems to be stuck where image generation was in 2016. Is there something else or is this just not a common need?

Feat: Gamification & Categorized XP System
### Summary

Expand Donetick’s existing point system to support **Gamification / XP Mode**, including custom **XP Categories** (e.g., *Health & Fitness*, *Learning*, *Chores*) and API endpoints to query user XP totals by type.

---

### 💡 Problem / Motivation

While Donetick currently supports basic points for tasks, standard points don't fully capture different domains of life or personal growth.

Categorized XP (Experience Points) turns task completion into an engaging gamified system. This helps:

* **Increase Engagement:** Gamification makes chores and habits fun for kids and adults alike.
* **Balanced Growth Tracking:** Categorizing tasks allows users to see *where* they spend their effort (e.g., mental vs. physical tasks).
* **Home Automation & Dashboarding:** API access to XP categories enables custom dashboards or smart-home rules (e.g., enabling access to rewards/devices only after earning required XP). this would closes #832 

---

###  Proposed Solution

#### 1. XP / Gamification Settings

* Add an option to toggle display terminology between **Points** and **XP**.
* Allow users/admins to define custom **XP Categories** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`, `Learning`, `Home & Household`).

#### 2. Task Configuration

* When creating/editing a task, allow choosing:
* **XP Value:** (e.g., `50 XP`)
* **XP Category:** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`)



#### 3. API & Integration Support

* Provide REST API endpoints to fetch user XP statistics:
* `GET /api/v1/users/{userID}/xp` – Returns total XP broken down by category.
* `GET /api/v1/circles/{circleID}/xp` – Returns group/circle leaderboard or category breakdown.


* *Example API Response:*
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "total_xp": 450,
  "categories": {
    "health_and_fitness": 200,
    "learning": 150,
    "chores": 100
  }
}

```



---

### Example Use Cases

1. **Custom Dashboards:** Display a RPG-style character sheet / radar chart on a smart display or Grafana showing current levels in different life stats.
2. **Smart Home Automations (Home Assistant):** Trigger an automation via Home Assistant (e.g., unlocking a smart lock on a snack drawer or enabling screen time) only after earning a required threshold of *Health & Fitness* or *Learning* XP.

---

P.S. I’m willing to place a $100 bounty on this feature if a maintainer or contributor is open to implementing it and the PR is accepted and merged.

Show HN: Lemma, an IDE for reading mathematics (macOS, open source)
I built Lemma while working through The Elements of Statistical Learning (using the Preview app). Kept running into references like "(3.41)" or "by Theorem 2.3" forcing me to scroll back through the entire book. And whenever a proof wasn’t detailed enough, I'd screenshot it, ask ChatGPT to explain, then go back to the PDF to add manual notes. Got pretty annoying. That led me to Lemma: it reads a PDF once (locally), lets you jump around between equations, theorems, etc. without constantly scrolling. I gave it a VS Code look because yes, I'm addicted to VS Code (there are other themes for normal people). A non-exhaustive list of things it can do (right now): - References to theorems, equations, figures, citations and index entries are all clickable (you can peek at them without leaving the page) - You can ask an agent or ChatGPT Web for explanations, longer proofs with one click, save the output in Lemma - When the pdf says “it is easy to show” or “proof left to the reader”, you can write the missing steps in LaTeX, and Lemma checks it on random numerical inputs and gives counterexamples if it’s wrong. You can also fold proofs to try them yourself first, and keep notes attached to specific passages (with exports to Markdown, Anki and Jupyter). Built in Swift/SwiftUI using PDFKit. The analysis runs in a helper process at low priority. No account, no telemetry, and it's GPL.
It’s for macOS 15+ only for now (unless a lot of people find it useful, then I’ll probably do it for other OSes).
It still struggles with some PDFs (scanned ones, other languages, different numbering, etc.) If you try it on whatever you're reading and encounter some problems, feel free to open an issue!

CHINA BENCHMARK / Connected-vehicle sourcing and BIS 2027/2030 legal gate
## Goal
Determine which Chinese-origin automotive technology, if any, can lawfully be used in a U.S. HAVEN production vehicle.

### Required work
- [ ] Engage U.S. trade and vehicle cybersecurity counsel before Chinese ADAS/AI/telematics software or platform procurement (founder approval required for spend).
- [ ] Review BIS January 2025 connected vehicle final rule at https://media.bis.gov/connected-vehicles and 15 CFR Part 791.
- [ ] Map MY2027 covered software and MY2030 VCS hardware restrictions; analyze supplier ownership/control and development origin.
- [ ] Identify exempt / permitted products and applicable authorizations; do **not** treat all China-manufactured commodities as banned.
- [ ] Compare US/EU/Japan/Korea-certified independent suppliers capable of comparable cabin AI, ADAS and core controller capabilities.
- [ ] Require audit trail, independent safety case, software provenance, cybersecurity update rights, warranty, source/toolchain access and field service.
- [ ] Record legal open questions, costs and decision owners privately.

### Acceptance
Qualified counsel's dated sourcing framework and product-module supplier eligibility matrix; status remains OPEN until review.

**No importation or contracts authorized.**

source_text:
Show HN: Singularity – memory that makes coding agents cheaper on repeat work
Coding agents start every session from zero. Ask Claude Code for a change like one it made last week and it reads the same files again, falls into the same test traps again, and you pay for all of it again. Singularity learns from your finished sessions (change committed, tests passing): where each kind of change goes in this repo, how it gets checked, and the mistakes made along the way. When the next task starts, a hook hands the agent the workflows that fit, pointed at the code as it is today. Picking them is plain text matching with no model call. It stores where to edit, never the code itself. Results, medians of 3–4 runs per side, hidden tests decide pass/fail, every run passed. On excalidraw: - A long task with four changes, all of kinds memory had learned: 1.9M → 423k tokens, $0.81 → $0.30, 28.5 → 9.5 turns. - The same kind of task, but two of the four changes were bugs it had never seen: 39% fewer tokens, 38% lower cost. The unseen bugs cost the same with or without memory. - Where it doesn't help: small tasks in validator.js and one-off bug fixes. The difference there is about zero, within noise. Each measurement was written down before it was run. The plans and results are in the repo. Caveats: 3–4 runs per side, mostly one repo. Only Claude Code sessions are learned from; Codex, Gemini CLI and Droid get the hand-over through their hooks. Learning uses your Claude account (about $0.25 a round, capped at $1 a day, and only if you opt in). Everything is stored locally in ~/.singularity. Install (Windows PowerShell and more options in the README):     curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pandacover/singularity/main/install.sh | sh
  
I'd love to hear where it breaks on your repos, and what memory should carry for one-off work like bug fixes.

source_text:
AI Assistant workflow save fails with empty sourceCode, overwrites SDK file
### Bug Description

The AI Assistant repeatedly failed to save changes to an existing workflow, despite successful TypeScript SDK validation.

The captured build-workflow calls included both a valid filePath and sourceCode: "". After a failed build, the referenced source file was confirmed to be 0 bytes.

The build returned:

Default export is not a workflow. Make sure your file has: export default workflow(...)

The Assistant retried the same approach multiple times, including after stating that it would omit sourceCode. The requested changes were never saved.

Impact
The requested scheduling and lookback changes were not saved. The existing live workflow remained unchanged, and no workflow execution was attempted.

### To Reproduce

Observed sequence:

Ask the AI Assistant to modify an existing workflow.
The Assistant exports it to a .workflow.ts workspace file and applies scoped edits.
SDK validation succeeds with “no issues found”.
The Assistant calls build-workflow with the file path and an empty sourceCode string.
The build fails with the error above.
Inspecting the workspace file shows that it is now 0 bytes.
The Assistant re-exports, edits, validates, and retries, but encounters the same failure.


### Expected behavior

When building from filePath, the Assistant should omit sourceCode and preserve the existing source file.

If an empty sourceCode value is supplied, the tool should reject it without overwriting the file, or otherwise handle it safely. After repeated identical failures, the Assistant should stop rather than repeat the same save approach.

source_text:
Shopify Flow: inventoryAdjustQuantities, Idempotency & Error Handling for Subscription Bundles
Hello Shopify Community! 
 I’m looking for technical guidance on a Shopify Flow workflow we’ve built for our small soap business. We’ve completed the workflow, but we’re holding off on activating it until we can confirm that inventory adjustments will execute reliably. 
  Our setup:  
 
 Shopify Basic plan 
 Appstle Subscriptions for recurring orders 
 Easify Product Options for customer soap selections 
 13 individual soap products with Shopify inventory tracking enabled 
 Three subscription bundles containing 4, 8, or 12 customer-selected bars 
 
  How our workflow operates:  
 
 Trigger:  Order created  
 Check whether the order has the  FPC-Inventory-Processed  tag. 
 Identify orders containing a Front Porch Club subscription product. 
 Loop through the order’s line items. 
 Identify the subscription line item. 
 Loop through its custom attributes ( Bar #1 ,  Bar #2 , etc.). 
 Match each selected soap name against 13 predefined conditions. 
 Use Shopify’s built-in  Send Admin API request  action with  inventoryAdjustQuantities  to deduct one unit from the corresponding product’s inventory. 
 
 Each soap is mapped to its Shopify Inventory Item ID and our fulfillment Location ID. 
 We’ve tested the workflow using Shopify Flow’s simulation. The conditions correctly identify the selected soaps and reach the appropriate API action. However, the API mutations cannot be simulated, so we haven’t verified the actual inventory adjustments. 
  We have three technical questions:  
  1. Idempotency  
 Our workflow uses API version  2026-07 . 
 The  inventoryAdjustQuantities  mutation requires an idempotency key using the  @idempotent  directive. 
 However, Flow’s built-in Send Admin API request action generates the GraphQL mutation automatically and only exposes an editor for the JSON mutation inputs. 
 Is there a supported way to provide the required idempotency key through this built-in action? 
 If not, does that mean  inventoryAdjustQuantities  cannot be reliably executed through Flow’s standard Admin API request action? 
  2. Accessing mutation errors  
 We understand that a GraphQL mutation can return  userErrors  even when the HTTP request itself succeeds. 
 We attempted to add a Condition immediately after the API request, but  userErrors  wasn’t available as a variable. 
 Can Shopify Flow access the  userErrors  returned by  inventoryAdjustQuantities ? 
 If so, what is the correct variable path or configuration? 
  3. Handling partial inventory adjustments  
 For a subscription containing multiple soaps, some adjustments could succeed before a subsequent request fails. 
 We want to avoid: 
 
 Deducting the same soap twice. 
 Marking an order processed when some adjustments failed. 
 Incorrect inventory counts when a workflow is retried. 
 Problems processing recurring Appstle subscription orders. 
 
 What is the recommended approach for safely handling these situations within Shopify Flow? 
  Our goal  
 Ideally, we’d like to keep this automation within Shopify Flow on our Basic plan rather than upgrade our plan or purchase another app. 
 We’re also open to a lightweight custom integration if the built-in Flow action cannot safely accomplish this. 
 Any guidance from developers familiar with Shopify Flow and the Admin GraphQL API would be greatly appreciated. 
  Thank you!
