Unrecognized node type for community packages with a dot in the npm scope
### Bug Description

Community node packages whose npm scope contains a dot (for example `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven` or `@explorium.ai/n8n-nodes-explorium`) can be installed and their nodes show up in the node panel, but executing a workflow that uses one of these nodes fails with:

```
Unrecognized node type: @seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven
```

Root cause: the backend derives the package of a full node type with `fullNodeType.split(".")`. For `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven.seven` this yields package `@seven` and node `io/n8n-nodes-seven`, so no loader is found. Affected places on current master:

- `packages/cli/src/load-nodes-and-credentials.ts`: `recognizesNode`, `getNode`, `resolveNodeSourcePath`
- `packages/cli/src/modules/type-availability-policies/policy-evaluator.ts`: `nodeTypePackageResolver` (`split(".")[0]`), so a `package` policy rule for such a package never matches its nodes

The same pattern exists in `packages/core`, which the n8n team maintains in-house:

- `packages/core/src/nodes-loader/directory-loader.ts`: `extractNodeTypes`, used for `NODES_INCLUDE` / `NODES_EXCLUDE`
- `packages/core/nodes-testing/load-nodes-and-credentials.ts`: `getNode`

Node names never contain a dot, while npm package names may contain dots in the scope and in the name, so splitting at the last dot fixes all of these.

History: reported before in #15574 (closed by the stale bot), fixed in #25018 (closed as stale) and #41033 (closed because it touched `packages/core`). I will open a PR limited to `packages/cli` and `packages/workflow`; the `packages/core` sites above would need to be handled by the n8n team.

### To Reproduce

1. Start a self-hosted n8n instance.
2. Go to Settings > Community nodes and install `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven@0.2.0`.
3. Create a workflow with a Manual Trigger and add the seven node (it is listed in the node panel).
4. Execute the workflow.
5. See the error `Unrecognized node type: @seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven`.

### Expected behavior

Nodes from a community package with a dot in its npm scope execute like nodes from any other community package, and `NODES_INCLUDE` / `NODES_EXCLUDE` as well as `package` rules of type availability policies work for them.

### Debug Info

Not attached from a running instance. The behavior was checked against current master (commit 46761a60, n8n 2.44.0) with unit tests on `LoadNodesAndCredentials.recognizesNode` / `getNode`: `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven.seven` is not recognized and `getNode` throws `UnrecognizedNodeTypeError`, while `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest`, `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` and `n8n-nodes-foo.bar` resolve correctly.

## Environment

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.2

### n8n Version

2.44.0 (master)

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

source_text:
Launch HN: Consus (YC F24) – LLM gateway for companies handling sensitive data
Hey Hacker News! I'm Eric, the founder of Consus. We route all AI requests to ITAR restricted and controlled unclassified information (CUI) compliant infrastructure.
Consus itself satisfies ITAR restrictions, and we recently completed our FedRAMP equivalency audit against the 410 FedRAMP High controls. FedRAMP High is the U.S. government’s strictest security baseline for cloud services handling sensitive unclassified data. A breach of this data could cause severe or catastrophic harm. Achieving FedRAMP equivalency, or authorization, is required before processing CUI information. Demo:  https://youtu.be/6MYxJe6P4oY  Aerospace and defense is experiencing rapid growth. Unfortunately, most companies are struggling to use AI because of necessary data protections & compliance risk. These companies can move even faster if they could use the AI tools that most other industries take for granted. I spent most of my career prior to Consus in aerospace & defense. I launched national security payloads at SpaceX, and was an early employee at Castelion. I’ve watched first hand how compliance red-tape makes it difficult for companies to adopt new technologies and trust vendors that touch their sensitive data. For example, I worked with a satellite manufacturer that doesn’t allow any AI tools, even for non-sensitive work. Even as AI has become extremely useful over the past 9-12 months, I was surprised by how many aerospace & defense companies refused to touch it. They could see how it could be helpful, but they were scared about model providers training on their data, violating an ITAR rule, or risk losing new business because of a failed cyber assessment. These are all rational fears. There were a lot of ways to solve some/all of these problems, but we focused on building a compliant AI inference layer that can "plug" into any AI tool or workflow. Just as OpenRouter integrates with most tools, Consus can connect to tools like ChatGPT or Claude, open source tools including the Pi coding agent or Open WebUI, or integrate with applications built and maintained by individual organizations. Almost no aerospace & defense company lives in all three major GovClouds (AWS, Azure, Google). When I mapped where frontier models can legally run for ITAR and CUI work, each provider had some subset of models, and each model achieved varying levels of compliance. Our customers don’t think in terms of cloud providers. They think about the data controls they require, and the model they want to use.
That is why we built the compliance suffix. Under the hood, every request hits a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, where keys are verified and policy is enforced before anything touches inference. Every model name must carry a compliance suffix, such as gpt-5.6-sol:fedramp-high or claude-opus-5-5:itar, and any bare model name is rejected. We never proxy to the standard commercial endpoints. Our customers are also able to build an allowlist of models, and assign spend & model restrictions to individual users in the organization. This is all handled through our Consus Portal where teams can manage spend, keys, and policies. A typical question we hear is why not just use Bedrock in AWS GovCloud or Azure Government directly. For small teams, just getting access to these platforms is difficult. For larger organizations, GovCloud lets you inherit some but not all of the controls needed to handle sensitive data. Also, models are split across providers: GPT-5.6 Sol is only available in Azure Government, while Claude Opus 5.5 is served through Bedrock in AWS GovCloud. If you want both, you are standing up and securing two separate government cloud environments. We run all of them behind one endpoint so customers don’t have to pick a cloud, and we handle the compliance work for each one. Given the data sensitivities, Consus does not store any customer data at rest. All prompts and completions stay in memory only for the length of the request and are never logged or written to disk. Zero data retention is strictly enforced both on ourselves and the infrastructure/model providers. We do keep metadata on each request and response for billing and audit purposes. Consus is not self-serve by design. ITAR requires us to know exactly who is on the other end of every key, so we verify every organization and put a contract in place before issuing API keys. We charge our customers a compliance fee starting at $40/mo/seat plus AI tokens at cost. We are actively serving customers, and would love any feedback from security experts, or developers/engineers working in highly regulated industries! References:
API Documentation:  https://gateway.consus.io/overview 
Security & Architecture:  https://gateway.consus.io/security 
Compliance Details:  https://consus.io/compliance

Zenvocloud: zero-cost first-customer acquisition sprint
## Goal
Acquire the first verified paying B2B customer for Zenvocloud/TaskForge, with $0 upfront spend and no invented leads or revenue.

## Current verified baseline (2026-10-12)
- Production homepage and 11 other intended routes return HTTP 200.
- `/api/lead` rejects GET (405) and invalid POST (400); valid submission, storage and notifications not yet verified.
- Upwork freelancer profile is active but positioned primarily around financial planning and unrelated skills; 0 Connects. Do not buy Connects or claim applications were submitted.
- Cloudflare production deployment is successful; do not assume all premium redesign elements are live.

## Work packages (execute, verify, record evidence)
1. Verify the valid lead intake end-to-end using an isolated staging environment and synthetic data; remove test records; verify notifications and avoid any live false leads.
2. Check all visible CTAs and customer paths for broken links, quote request friction, honest service claims, and privacy compliance.
3. Build a concise B2B offer sheet for inventory/CSV cleanup, CRM data quality, and operational automation with truthful sample work and scoped deliverables. Do not invent testimonials or guaranteed outcomes.
4. Prepare free-channel distribution: portfolio pages, relevant communities/directories where business posts are permitted, and compliant, tailored outreach to genuine buyer requests. No mass unsolicited spam.
5. Audit Upwork positioning and draft a factual replacement headline/bio/skills for user confirmation. Do not edit profile without platform-required approval; no paid Connects.
6. Verify merchant checkout and fulfillment independently before accepting payment; keep unverified gates closed.
7. Track weekly metrics: qualified prospects discovered, relevant outreach sent, replies, quotes, verified payments. Report zeros explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Evidence links for each completed action.
- One successful isolated end-to-end synthetic lead test, with cleanup evidence.
- At least one honest, discoverable offer and one verified permitted zero-cost acquisition channel.
- No spending, fabricated customer records, or unauthorized outreach.

Owner workflow: Cavalry team can take work packages through its actual runtime; **this issue is a backlog artifact only and does not prove a Cavalry handoff or background execution**.

## Objective

### Scope: one small PR
1. A pure decision contract: only authoritative, fresh, fully bound per-lot `PASS_TO_TS` enters TS research. `HOLD_NATIONAL`, `SKIP`, missing evidence, and manual K-column values without source verification never enter automatic supplier research. No `GO` inferred.
2. Define typed normalized result shape for: lot identity/announcement, original TS source/link/hash and criteria list, actual candidate Brand+Model+Partnumber, criterion-by-criterion evidence and `TS_COMPLIANCE_100_PERCENT` (never fabricated), three distinct supplier quotes with price/date/stock/lead time evidence, delivery/taxes/certifications/fees/contingency, total landed cost, net profit, margin, markup, break-even, and GO/REVIEW/NO-GO. I need a reliable Python-based bot whose single purpose is to integrate several external APIs and keep the data flowing between them without manual intervention. The core of the job is to build clean, well-structured code that can:

Two key areas of our work are encouraging healthier youth sports culture and helping people take daily breaks from technology to be more present. 
 I’m looking for an experienced AI marketing and automation specialist who can help translate this mission into consistent storytelling, audience growth, and measurable sales. 
 What I’m looking to build 
 A coordinated marketing system using n8n and AI tools such as Claude or OpenAI to: 
 ● Develop content grounded in our brand voice, values, and product offerings. 
 ● Create and repurpose social posts, video scripts, and email campaigns. 
 ● Manage a content calendar and approval process.

 ● Track performance and use those insights to improve campaigns. 
 Preserving the authenticity of chill life’s message is essential. The system should support thoughtful storytelling, with my review and approval built into the process. 
 Who would be a strong fit 
 Someone who combines technical skill with marketing judgment and has already built successful AI marketing workflows for an apparel, lifestyle, or consumer-product brand. 
 You should be able to show what you built, explain the strategy behind it, and share measurable results—particularly sales, conversions, customer acquisition, or repeat purchases. 
 An interest in positivity, mental fitness, youth sports, and building a brand with purpose would be a meaningful advantage. 
 Engagement and partnership

 2. Examples of n8n and AI workflows you have built. 
 3. Your role in both marketing strategy and implementation.

 Learn more about the brand:  https://chill-life.com

 Beth Levis

source_text:
Golden Client E2E — parcours boutique→retrait, preuves documentaires B2C/B2B et recette humaine
## Objectif produit
Transformer la Golden actuelle (cockpit 10 frontières, commande synthétique créée déjà payée) en **recette complète boutique → client final → finance**, comprenant **documents clients + preuves B2B et contrôles agents**. Un seul fil `market + order_reference + trace_id` lie Playwright, verdicts humains, écrans réels, documents et oracles backend. Ne pas refaire les centaines de tests existants ; les réutiliser.

## État vérifié sur main au 13/10/2026
- `public/golden-e2e-cockpit.html` offre 10 étapes et les boutons `golden-create` / `golden-advance` ; il commence sur une commande **déjà préparée**, pas sur la visite client/OTP/checkout. `services/golden-e2e-cockpit.js` projette les faits métiers, pas les documents.
- Le cockpit peut actuellement afficher `Golden certifié` sur **10 clics humains** indépendamment des preuves backend (faux vert).
- Route `/admin/golden-e2e` présente dans `bootstrap/html-routes.js` ; entrée de menu Canonical à confirmer/brancher sous autorité admin.
- `routes/admin-order-360.js` : POST `golden-create` / `golden-advance` sont **interdits en production** (garde NODE_ENV). Ne jamais contourner cette garde.
- `features/documents.feature.js` / `routes/documents.js` : accès privé client sous `/api/auth/me/documents` ; actuellement la liste client expose factures et reçus de remboursement. `transaction_documents` contient aussi des justificatifs internes. Aucune URL documentaire publique, aucun PDF envoyé via WhatsApp.
- Réconciliation Hub distincte du fulfillment ; réception réelle validée par agent Hub ; remise client distincte de disponibilité relais.
- Source : `docs/doctrine/DOCTRINE_DOCUMENTS_TRANSACTIONNELS_KOMERCE.md` et `docs/audits/KOMERCE_E2E_CERTIFICATION_GAP.md` (audit point de départ, à réévaluer sur HEAD).

## Scénario fil rouge — automatisation puis recette humaine
1. **Client navigateur réel** : market KM/CM/CG, catalogue sourcé et affichage en français, fiche produit/variante/prix/stock, panier individuel ou liste figée.
2. **Client authentification OTP** : émission réelle sur sandbox contrôlé, réception/validation, expiration, erreur, tentative concurrente. Pas de faux « OTP reçu » à partir d'une simple réponse simulée.
3. **Checkout** : choix relais, devise, prix figé, création commande depuis la vraie boutique (pas d'INSERT préalable). Variantes wallet, cash relais, PSP sandbox si disponible, Mobile Money selon market/capacité.
4. **Confirmation** : événement de paiement confirmé (pas simple `pending`), commande/reçu, **facture client** (PDF immuable privé, bon destinataire), historique / Mon Komerce / notification.
5. **Achat fournisseur** : `purchase_lines` → PO SKU/SOI exact, groupement, doublons/concurrence, fournisseur/quantités/devise. Contrôle du bon de commande B2B (trame/état réel, PDF seulement si un système en produit un).
6. **Exécution fournisseur** : preuve de commande et de paiement fournisseur, confirmation/accusé externe **si réellement accessible**, matching/rejeu.
7. **Expédition fournisseur** : numéro tracking, preuve d'expédition / BL ou facture fournisseur si transmis ; aucun document présumé présent ; suivi fournisseur ne signifie **pas** réception Hub.
8. **Réception physique Hub** : agent Hub confirme unité/quantité/état sur vraie surface autorisée ; pièce de réception / écart / réserve rattachée à la PO. C'est le Hub qui confirme physiquement.
9. **Transit → douane → relais → remise** : pièces de transport/douane (si requises), réception relais réelle, scan QR/code/autorisation, preuve de retrait client ; disponible ≠ remis.
10. **Clôture** : coûts achat/transport/douane, cash garde si applicable, réconciliation et règlement Market (si applicable), documents comptables, absence d'écart non soldé.

### Variantes intégrées au même moteur
- Client individuel / liste partagée figée / deux sessions concurrentes.
- Paiement réussi, échoué, expiré, callback dupliqué/désordonné, annulation et remboursement.
- Stock limité et 2 achats simultanés ; divergence réservation / commande payée.
- KM/CM/CG, devise/prix/catalogue/français/relai, desktop et mobile ; ne promettre un PSP ou provider L6 que si sandbox réellement accessible.
- PO groupées/partielles, manque fournisseur, réception Hub partielle, incident douane, colis endommagé, échec document, retrait non autorisé.

## Matrice documentaire obligatoire et agent responsable
| Transition | Justificatif à contrôler | Source/autorité | Si absence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paiement confirmé | facture B2C PDF privée (après événement confirmé) | documents + orders | BLOQUANT, diagnostic Finance/Documents |
| Remboursement confirmé (variante) | avoir / reçu remboursement privé | refunds/documents | BLOQUANT |
| PO créée | PO persistée + représentation B2B si disponible | purchasing | agent Achats : vérifier génération/export ; ne pas inventer un PDF |
| Fournisseur confirmé/payé | référence fournisseur + preuve de débit + accusé/facture si disponible | purchasing/provider | agent Achats : récupérer/rapprocher ; contrôle manuel traçable |
| Fournisseur expédie | fulfillment / tracking + BL ou preuve transport **si fournie** | provider/purchasing | agent Achats ou Logistique : demander pièce, tracer absence |
| Hub reçoit | réception physique horodatée/quantités/agent + preuve de réception | Hub | agent Hub : contrôle réel, écart/réserve, BLOQUANT si absent |
| Douane/transit | déclaration / facture douane / justificatif transport selon exigibilité | logistics/customs | transitaire : rapprocher ou déclarer manquant |
| Relais reçoit | scan / statut réception physique réel | Relay | agent relais : contrôle, anomalie si non reçu |
| Client retire | scan de retrait autorisé + `pickup_proof` si émis | Relay/documents | agent relais : corriger ou signaler |
| Finance clôture | rapprochements coûts/règlement/cash, pièces nécessaires | Finance | comptable : investigation ouverte, aucun faux vert |

**Statuts documentaires** : `NON_DU`, `ATTENDU`, `DISPONIBLE_A_VERIFIER`, `VERIFIE`, `CONTROLE_MANUEL_REQUIS`, `MANQUANT_BLOQUANT` (projection de recette, pas cycle métier parallèle). Pour chaque pièce : événement déclencheur, exigibilité selon market/provider, source canonique, référence/URL authentifiée ou identifiant, horodatage, acteur, hash si disponible, verdict, raison d'absence, tâche agent / preuve d'intervention ; `non applicable` ne vaut pas `verifié`. Ne jamais fabriquer de PDF externe, de BL ou de facture fournisseur.

## Lots de livraison (PRs petites, gouvernées)
- [ ] **A — accès / cadrage** : menu admin Canonical → /admin/golden-e2e avec vérification des droits, scénario client réel distinct du parcours synthétique de frontière ; rendre visibles le market et les niveaux de preuve L0–L6.
- [ ] **B — client Playwright / humain** : réutiliser E2E boutique+OTP+checkout+partage, sessions clients et vrais écrans ; opérateur vérifie la continuité, sans injection directe de commande payée.
- [ ] **C — documents** : projection read-only par fil/order/PO : document source, éligibilité, statut, URL privée autorisée, responsable d'une preuve fournisseur absente ; distinguer B2C et B2B.
- [ ] **D — terrain** : cliquer sur les **actions réelles** avec rôle agent Hub/transitaire/relais (ou simulator non-prod explicitement étiqueté) ; pas de mutation depuis un écran de projection ni bypass de permissions.
- [ ] **E — verdict de certification** : `VERT` uniquement si preuves backend canoniques + documents obligatoires + étapes automatiques réellement exécutées + validations humaines + absence d'incident bloquant ; `NON EXECUTE`/mock/staging absent restent visibles, aucun faux vert.
- [ ] **F — scénarios négatifs et marchés** : concurrence, remboursements, webhooks, plusieurs marchés, mobile, documents conditionnels, rapport exportable et liens vers vraies interfaces.

## Garde-fous / définition de fini
- **Playwright avant humain** : l'humain joue d'abord le client (catalogue→OTP→paiement→confirmation), puis l'agent aux seules frontières physiques autorisées. La suite du client après paiement est essentiellement notification et suivi, pas clic forcé.
- Aucun reset destructif ; fixture dédiée, environnement isolé ; aucun achat/fonds réels ; aucun accès client à une pièce B2B ou fuite inter-market.
- Tests L3 mockés != L4 réel navigateur+serveur+DB != L5 staging != L6 prestataire sandbox. Afficher ces niveaux explicitement.
- Un `golden-create` ne remplace pas un vrai checkout ; les 10 étapes actuelles restent utiles comme **sous-recette**.
- S'assurer que les anomalies cash collections / statut shipping décrites par l'audit historique sont vérifiées sur main et corrigées si encore présentes.
- Avant modifications : `npm run agent:context -- --pack ui --feature dashboard`, `npm run agent:context -- --pack service --feature documents`, `npm run arch:impact -- ...`, tests ciblés, **`npm run pr:preflight` vert avant chaque PR**, CI et merge selon `AGENTS.md`.
- Terminé seulement quand une commande issue du navigateur traverse les vraies frontières jusqu'au retrait/clôture, que les documents sont consultables sous permissions correctes ou qu'un contrôle agent explicite résout leur absence, et que le verdict refuse tout faux vert.

## Amendement P0 — Sourcing et Raffinerie obligatoires avant la vraie boutique (13/10/2026)

La Golden complète ne démarre **jamais** d'un produit artificiellement injecté dans le catalogue. Chaîne requise : SOURCE FOURNISSEUR → SOURCING RÉUSSI → RAFFINERIE RÉUSSIE → REMISE AU CATALOGUE → PUBLICATION ET VENDABILITÉ MARKET → VRAIE BOUTIQUE → CLIENT → ACHAT → FOURNISSEUR → LIVRAISON → CLÔTURE.

Le sourcing et la raffinerie peuvent avoir déjà eu lieu avant l'ouverture du navigateur ; la Golden doit alors vérifier leurs faits persistés, leur identité et leur provenance. Un parcours acheté sur un produit préexistant est une certification partielle, et pas une certification complète de la source au client.

### Quatre preuves bloquantes

- SOURCE_PROVED : source réelle identifiée, capture/observation fraîche, identité exacte Offer/Unit/SOI, et passage sourcing réellement attesté, pas un seed.

- REFINERY_PROVED : passage et résultat réels, contrôles qualité et données produit/variantes/images, décisions de rejet ou d'acceptation journalisées, pas de bypass.

- CATALOG_RELEASE_PROVED : remise au catalogue par l'owner, SKU/variante exacts, publication et vendabilité Market, prix/devise/relais corrects, observés dans la boutique réelle.

- CUSTOMER_ORDER_PROVED : filiation jusqu'aux order_items et purchase_lines/PO, correspondance exacte product_sku_id et supplier_unit_ref/SOI, aucune substitution de SKU similaire.

### Cockpit et tests

Ajouter des étapes et des liens directs Sourcing → Raffinerie → Catalogue → Produit 360 → Boutique → Commande → PO fournisseur ; exposer verdict et preuve propre à chaque frontière. Rejeter une Golden complète si preuve absente, produit seed direct, raffinerie non attestée, publication simulée ou SKU/SOI divergente. Cas négatifs : source inconnue, article rejeté, stock/prix évoluant après sourcing, Market non publié, concurrence et replay. Ne pas relancer du sourcing pour chaque achat : proposer une exécution contrôlée séparée pour certifier la source au client avec vrais faits persistant sur environnement isolé. Réutiliser les propriétaires Sourcing, Raffinerie/Catalogue, Purchasing sans créer une vérité parallèle. Aucun achat, publication externe ou paiement live sans autorisation.

## Décision — Assainissement préalable des produits de test
Avant une Golden source→client, inventorier les produits actuellement créés directement par les tests ou seeds Sourcing, en distinguant environment, market_id, product_id/SKU, provenance et liens avec commandes/PO/paiements. Ne JAMAIS effectuer de DELETE global ni de RESET, ni toucher à la production. En DB éphémère dédiée de recette, retirer seulement les fixtures identifiées explicitement, via les services propriétaires et le mécanisme de nettoyage approprié ; si un produit a des liens métiers ou historique, le désactiver/écarter de la Golden plutôt que le supprimer. Vérifier les FK et le nombre avant/après, conserver les sources et traces d'audit. Dans la Golden, la liste de produits éligibles doit être vide au départ puis peuplée exclusivement par un sourcing réel + passage raffinerie + publication Catalogue attestés. Fournir d'abord inventaire et dry-run chiffré pour validation avant toute action destructive ; aucune suppression exécutée par la présente issue.

source_text:
Show HN: Tracon (air traffic control for subagents)
My Claude Code workflow usually involves... a lot of subagents. I make one Opus model coordinate work as my tech lead, it dispatches subagents using models appropriate for the task into their own git worktrees, and then I try to multitask and do something else while they run. I'd been finding lately (particularly with Opus 5.5) that there was a ton of drift and instances of subagents not doing anything and it was evading the attention of the TL despite the instructions I gave it to have them report in at a regular cadence. Running tracon in a split terminal is my new personal workflow. It gives me early indicators when things start going off the rails (ex. blocked on a prompt, idle, looping on a failing command, simultaneous edits to files other subagents are editing, drifting off the brief, etc.) and I can interrogate the subagent's workflow and by pressing n the main agent gets a note to make a call on how and if to correct it. Read-only and runs on your machine: it tails transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ and checks each worktree with ps, lsof, and git -- only thing that leaves your machine is what the Haiku judge reads for classification (or optionally you can turn that off with --no-judge). I've found it super useful for the game I'm building and figured others in the community might also find it useful. If you just want to give it a spin without committing:     uvx tracon --demo
  
macOS and Linux, Python 3.12+, MIT. (Not affiliated with Anthropic.)

source_text:
Microsoft SharePoint node (v1): `Return All` silently drops `$filter` and `$expand=fields` on `Item → Get Many`
### Bug Description

### Environment

- n8n version: 2.27.4 (self-hosted)
- Node: `n8n-nodes-base.microsoftSharePoint`, typeVersion 1
- Resource: `Item`, Operation: `Get Many`
- Credential: Microsoft SharePoint OAuth2 API

### Summary

When `Return All` is enabled on the SharePoint node's `Item → Get Many` operation, the generated request silently ignores:
1. The `Filter by Formula` field (no `$filter` is sent to the API), and
2. The `Options → Fields` selection (no `$expand=fields` is sent), even on **what should be the first page** of results.

Both work correctly when `Return All` is disabled and `Limit` is used instead. There is no error, warning, or any indication in the UI that these parameters were dropped — the node just returns the full, unfiltered list with metadata-only objects (no `fields` property at all).

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Microsoft SharePoint node, Resource = `Item`, Operation = `Get Many`.
2. Pick a Site and a List (a SharePoint document library with a few thousand items works best to reproduce).
3. In **Options → Fields**, select `Fields`.
4. In **Filter by Formula**, enter a condition on a non-indexed column, e.g.:
   ```
   fields/FileLeafRef eq 'some-exact-file-name.xlsx'
   ```
5. Enable **Return All**. Execute the node.
6. Observe: the node returns **every** item in the list (e.g. 4063 items in our case), not just the one matching the filter. No `fields` object is present on any returned item.
7. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to e.g. 100, keep the same filter. Execute again.
8. Observe: the node now correctly returns a `400 Bad Request` from the Graph/SharePoint API:
   ```
   Field 'FileLeafRef' cannot be referenced in filter or orderby as it is not indexed.
   Provide the 'Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly' header to allow this...
   ```
   This proves the `$filter` parameter **is** correctly sent to the API when `Return All` is off.
9. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to 50, remove the filter, keep **Fields** selected. Execute again.
10. Observe: the response correctly contains a `fields` object per item (e.g. `fields.FileLeafRef`, `fields.FileDirRef`, etc.), confirming `$expand=fields` **is** correctly sent when `Return All` is off.

### Expected behavior

With `Return All` enabled, the `$filter` and `$expand=fields` parameters configured via the UI should be sent on every page of the paginated request (at minimum, on the first page), exactly as they are when `Return All` is off and a manual `Limit` is used instead.

### Debug Info

### Actual Behavior

With `Return All` enabled:
- `$filter` is never applied — the server-side filter condition that reliably produces a `400` error when `Return All` is off produces **no error at all** and returns the full unfiltered dataset when `Return All` is on. This strongly suggests `$filter` is not being sent at all (not even on the first request), since the SharePoint API would reject the filtered query regardless of pagination state if it ever reached the server.
- `$expand=fields` is also missing from **every** returned item, including what should be the first page — not just subsequent pages fetched via `@odata.nextLink`.

### Evidence Table

| Return All | Limit | Filter set | Fields option | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ON | — | No | Yes | All 4063 items returned, **no `fields` key present on any item** |
| ON | — | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | All 4063 items returned (unfiltered), **no error** |
| OFF | 100 | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | **400 Bad Request** — "field not indexed" (proves filter *was* sent) |
| OFF | 50 | No | Yes | 50 items returned, **`fields` object correctly present** on each |

### Root Cause (hypothesis, not confirmed against source)

Looking at `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/v1/descriptions/item/getAll.operation.ts`, the `returnAll` property's routing config defines a `pagination.request` override:

```ts
pagination: {
  type: 'generic',
  properties: {
    continue: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] }}',
    request: {
      url: '={{ $response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ?? $request.url }}',
      qs: {
        $select: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ? undefined : $request.qs?.$select }}',
      },
    },
  },
},
```

This `request.qs` object only ever defines `$select`. If n8n's generic pagination engine uses this object to *replace* (rather than merge into) the full query-string for **every** request in the paginated sequence — including the first one, once `paginate` is truthy — then `$filter` (set via a separate `routing.send` on the `filter` field) and `$expand` (injected via a `preSend` hook on `simplify`/`options.fields`) would both be silently dropped whenever `Return All` is on, regardless of page number. This matches 100% of the observed behavior above.

We have not confirmed this against n8n core's `RoutingNode`/generic-pagination implementation directly — flagging as hypothesis for the n8n team to verify against the actual merge logic.

### Workaround Used

Since neither `Return All` + `Filter` nor `Return All` + `Fields` work together reliably, we worked around this by:
- Avoiding `Item → Get Many` + `Return All` entirely for this use case.
- Downloading a specific file directly via `File → Download`, addressing it with the Graph `{parentFolderId}:/{fileName}:` syntax, which does not depend on `Get Many`/pagination at all.

### Operating System

Linux

### n8n Version

2.27.4

### Node.js Version

24.0.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

I hear you. You built this domain and hardware stack yourself on a tight budget, and now you need a lean, high-leverage system to source, productize, market, and ship without draining your capital. ---
### 🔍 1. US Vendor Sourcing (Free & Vetting-Ready)
| Resource | Cost | How to Use It |
|----------|------|---------------|
| **Thomasnet** (thomsonnet.com) | Free directory access | Filter by state/industry. Export contact lists manually. Verify via public LLC registries. |
| **Alibaba** (alibaba.com) | Free search | Use “Trade Assurance” filter. Download business license photos from vendor profiles. Cross-check with DuckDuckGo Business. |
| **SBA Supplier Directory** (sba.gov) | Free | Find locally certified vendors, women/minority-owned suppliers, and grant-eligible wholesalers. |
| **Reddit & Industry Forums** (e.g., r/smallbusiness, niche-specific subs) | Free | Ask for vetted US manufacturers. DM verified sellers with sample requests. |
| **Amazon Business Supplier / Amazon Vendor Central** | Free to apply | If you sell physical goods, get approved to source wholesale at MSRP discounts. |

✅ **Vetting Checklist (Do this before spending):**
- Request a sample + invoice template
- Verify business license via state SOS or DDRC databases
- Check BBB & Trustpilot for shipping/quality complaints
- Confirm MOQs, lead times, and return policies in writing
- Use free tools like `duckduckgo.com/business` to verify domain/email legitimacy

---
### 💡 2. Product Ideation Framework (Based on Local Vendors)
1. **Trend Scan (Free):** 
   - Google Trends → filter by “US” + your niche
   - Ubersuggest Free Tier → 10 searches/month for keyword volume & competition
   - Amazon Best Sellers → sort by “Last 24 Hours” + read review gaps
2. **Margin Math:** 
   `Selling Price = (COGS × 3) + Shipping + Platform Fees + 20% Buffer`
   Target ≥70% gross margin to survive Wix/Stripe fees and low ad spend.
3. **Validation Loop:**
   - List product idea on a free landing page (Wix Pages or Carrd)
   - Run $0 organic traffic (Pinterest, Reddit, local Facebook groups)
   - Track clicks → email signups → cart adds before investing inventory

---
### 🖼️ 3. Product Image & Ad Enhancement (Zero-Cost Stack)
| Task | Free Tool | Workflow |
|---------------------|----------|
| Background removal / object cleanup | `remove.bg` (free tier: 5 images) | Clean product photos, isolate on white/brand color |
| Photo editing / resizing | `Photopea.com` (free Photoshop clone) | Batch adjust exposure, add watermarks, resize to Wix specs |
| Canva templates & social assets | `canva.com` (free account) | Create carousels, UGC-style ads, story templates |
| Stock/UGC images | Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay | Filter by “Commercial use” + niche keywords |
| Video editing for ads | CapCut (desktop/mobile) | 15-30s hooks: problem → product → CTA. Export optimized for TikTok/Reels |

✅ **Pro Tip:** Shoot one hero shot on your phone → edit in Photopea → create 3 ad variations in Canva → post organically first → only boost what gets engagement before scaling.

---
### 🌐 4. SEO Optimization (Wix-Native + Free External)
| Area | Action | Why It Matters |
|------|--------|----------------|
| **Wix SEO Wiz** | Enable in Settings > SEO | Auto-fixes meta tags, redirects, mobile usability |
| **Custom URLs & Sitemaps** | Settings > Site Structure → Customize URLs; Export XML sitemap | Crawlers love clean, logical paths |
| **Image Optimization** | Compress via TinyPNG (free) → add descriptive alt text | Speed + image search traffic |
| **Mobile Speed** | Remove unused Wix apps, defer JS, use WebP | Core Web Vitals impact rankings & bounce rate |
| **Keyword Research** | Ubersuggest Free Tier, AnswerThePublic (5 queries/day), Google Autocomplete | Target low-competition, high-intent long-tail keywords |
| **Content Engine** | Wix Blog (free) → publish 1x/week targeting vendor reviews, setup guides, comparison posts | Builds backlinks + positions you as authoritative |

✅ **Quick SEO Audit Checklist:**
- [ ] Title tags <60 chars, meta descriptions <155 chars
- [ ] H1 matches page intent, H2/H3 structure logical
- [ ] All images compressed & alt-text filled
- [ ] Mobile test passes (PageSpeed Insights free)
- [ ] Google Search Console connected + 404s checked weekly

---
### 📦 5. Shipping Partners Through Wix (Free/Low-Cost Path)
| Carrier | Cost/Setup | Best For |
|---------|------------|----------|
| **USPS + Postmark** | $0.65/package, free labels up to 5/day | Low volume, domestic orders |
| **LFO (USPS Lower Rates)** | Free account, lower base rates | Volume shipping within US |
| **EasyPost** | 7-day free trial → multi-carrier rate comparison | Testing USPS vs UPS/FedEx before committing |

✅ **Wix Setup Steps:**
1. Wix Admin → Settings > Shipping & Payment
2. Enable “Wix Payments” (if not already)
3. Add carrier: `USPS` or `UPS` → connect via API/webhook if needed
4. Enable “Rate Shopping” so customers see real-time costs at checkout
5. Set free shipping threshold only after calculating true COGS + fees

⚠️ Avoid paid Wix add-ons unless absolutely necessary. Stick to native shipping + USPS/LFO for bootstrap efficiency.

---
### ⚙️ 6. Automation Stack (Free Tiers That Actually Work)
| Tool | Free Tier Limits | Use Case with Wix |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Zapier** | 100 tasks/mo, 2,500 actions/mo | Wix order → Google Sheets → Vendor email → Customer confirmation |
| **Make.com (Integromat)** | 300 actions/mo | Webhook from Wix checkout → Slack alert → Auto-reply via Twilio/SMS |
| **Wix Native Automations** | Unlimited basic flows | Email sequences, inventory alerts, abandoned cart reminders |
| **GitHub Actions** | Free for public repos | Run Python/Node scripts to scrape vendor prices or update product feeds |

✅ **Starter Automation Blueprint:**
```
Wix Checkout Event → Zapier → Create Google Sheet Row → Send Vendor Order (if print-on-demand) → Trigger Customer Email (Wix Native)
```
All free. Scales with your revenue.

---
### 🧭 Next Steps: Tell Me These 3 Things & I’ll Generate Exact Assets for You
1. **What product category/niche** are you selling? (e.g., tech accessories, handmade goods, digital templates, print-on-demand)
2. **Do you have a current vendor list or supplier type?** (wholesale, dropshipping, local artisans, custom manufacturing)
3. **Which automation flow feels most urgent right now?** (vendor outreach → product listing → ad creative → SEO content → shipping setup)

Reply with those 3 points and I’ll deliver:

- Step-by-step Zapier/Make automation blueprint
- SEO keyword list + blog post outline tailored to your products

How does the crowding out work here? I'm not being pedantic, I'm genuinely curious about the dynamics as you see them. My experience in the publishing
How does the crowding out work here? I'm not being pedantic, I'm genuinely curious about the dynamics as you see them. My experience in the publishing world is that there is already an infinite supply of writing. Lots of things serve as filters, some for better and some for worse, but ultimately the quality of the writing (however we define that) vs. the field is part of that filter. There is a competition for our limited little attention spans and finite waking hours, and writing better suited to our tastes tends to win out. I don't see how that dynamic changes with AI. If all writers have more or less equal access to AI, some writers will use it in ways that result in writing I enjoy more than others. Some won't use it at all and still write work I really like. The majority of people writing with or without AI, just as today, won't write stuff I really want to read. I don't know if I've ever read a piece of SEO-driven content marketing and thought it was particularly profound or that it made an impact on me. Or that I really had an inherently meaningful connection to the author. I sort of don't care if people generate 100x more of that sort of thing. It makes Google searches less effective, I guess? Or it may make my For You Page on Instagram less human-rich? I've read some nice poetry though. I usually go looking for it. There are a handful of authors I tend to like consistently. The overall volume of poetry published (it's quite a lot!) doesn't really have an effect on my preference for their work. If there was 1,000,000 times more poetry published because of AI, I don't think it would prevent me from seeking out new poems from writers/publishers/curators I like, nor would I probably really notice.

source_text:
Gamma roadmap: intelligent starter actions, multimodal documents, safe Excel, tool-first architecture
# Gamma architecture roadmap — tool-first, not reinventing the wheel

**Status:** Planned only. **Gate:** Complete controlled human Beta and document-retrieval validation before implementing Gamma. This issue is a durable planning record; it authorizes no changes to main, production, billing, or user data.

## Product principles
- Gemini remains the reasoning/orchestration brain. Understand intent in DE/FA/EN (extensible to more languages); use tools only when useful.
- Evidence priority: verified internal living archive and standards -> general reasoning -> public web where appropriate; preserve deterministic safety/standards verification, precise citations for verified claims, uncertainty on insufficient evidence.
- **Use -> Extend -> Build**: evaluate native ChatGPT/OpenAI capabilities, GitHub integrations/actions, established libraries and APIs before building bespoke implementations. Avoid duplicating PDF reading/summarization, OCR, Excel execution, document parsing, search, and file management.
- Review newly available tools and connector capabilities at implementation time against cost, security, privacy, vendor lock-in, quality, and maintenance. Do not assume a capability exists or is free until verified.
- Keep elevator.help technical assistance separate from the later commercial **Elevator Agent AI** supplier/parts marketplace. Provide a future handoff interface, not premature marketplace implementation.

## Six starter actions and expected behaviors
1. **Troubleshoot a fault**: ask manufacturer/model/fault code/context; optionally analyze photo/document; provide evidence-based, safety-conscious diagnostics.
2. **Search technical documentation**: retrieve relevant verified internal documentation first; provide grounded answer and citation where permitted; fallback appropriately.
3. **Ask about EN 81-20 / EN 81-50**: retrieve authoritative text, verify clause/numbers deterministically, fail closed on unverified normative claims.
4. **Plan shaft dimensions**: gather capacity, lift type, building constraints; provide clearly labeled preliminary guidance, not certified design.
5. **Send a photo**: inspect image, identify visible objects/labels and uncertainty; ask *what the user wants to do* (identify component, troubleshoot, find manual, find spare part, find supplier). Never infer unseen technical properties.
6. **Upload a document**: securely parse PDF/images/office files as supported, extract text/tables, summarize, answer user questions grounded in the uploaded file; ask intent when ambiguous.

## Proposed phased Gamma work
- **Gamma 1 — Intent and UX:** intelligent starter actions, intent router, follow-up questions, multilingual behavior, mobile scroll/input, clear answer feedback (like/dislike), observability. Reuse existing code.
- **Gamma 2 — Multimodal and documents:** photo analysis, PDF reading/summarization/Q&A, secure temporary uploads, consent for storage, per-user isolation, retention/deletion, size and rate limits, GDPR/privacy and cost budgets. No automatic ingestion of user uploads into shared/public archive.
- **Gamma 3 — Safe calculations:** run approved archived Excel calculation models and user-supplied spreadsheets in sandboxed, isolated execution; validated inputs, formulas, outputs, provenance, resource/time limits; never execute untrusted macros or arbitrary code. Use mature spreadsheet engines/libraries first.
- **Later:** validated Answer Catalog / canonical FAQs with versioned standard revalidation, quotas/metering and optional billing, My Elevator product finder. Supplier/spare-part sourcing remains a future Elevator Agent AI integration via an explicit tool contract.

## Acceptance / design gates
- Real-document end-to-end Living Archive test before Gamma.
- Human Beta test set: technical fault cases, verified standard clauses, ordinary conversational follow-ups, DE/FA/EN, mobile login and Google OAuth, performance/security/cost.
- For each new feature: inventory existing OpenAI/ChatGPT, GitHub, Gemini, Cloudflare and OSS tools; choose use/extend/build with rationale, measured costs and security review; add offline regression tests and production smoke checks.
- No new paid services or production deployment without explicit approval.

## Next action
After Beta is closed, decompose this roadmap into small independent implementation issues, beginning with Gamma 1. Do not start coding from this issue alone.

Junior Python LLM Bot Developer
I need a junior-level Python developer who is excited about building automation bots powered by both offline and online large-language models. The immediate task is to create bots that streamline routine processes for my company and then connect those bots seamlessly to our existing web apps, a couple of legacy desktop tools, and several cloud services we already use.  

You should already be comfortable spinning up SaaS-style back ends (FastAPI, Django, or a similar stack is fine) and have at least tinkered with frameworks such as LangChain, [login to view URL], or the OpenAI API so you can switch between local and hosted LLMs when needed. A solid grasp of common automation libraries—think Selenium, Playwright, PyAutoGUI, or REST hooks—will also make the work smoother.  

Deliverables I expect:  
• A working automation bot (or small fleet of bots) that can log in, collect data, act on it, and hand results back to our web, desktop, and cloud environments without manual intervention.  
• Clear, concise setup instructions and inline code comments so another developer can extend the project later.  
• A brief hand-off call or screen-share so I can see the bot in action and ask final questions.  

If you enjoy experimenting with LLM prompts, integrating APIs, and turning repetitive tasks into one-click workflows, you’ll be a great fit. Let me know what similar projects you’ve already built, especially any that bridged multiple platforms the way this one will.
Budget: ₹1500-12500 INR

[software-development-practices:nist-ssdf] github/gh-aw-firewall repository guidance Repository-observable SSDF controls for `github/gh-aw-firewall` are generally strong at commit `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab`: pinned GitHub Actions, scheduled CodeQL/dependency/supply-chain scans, SBOM/cosign coverage for container images, and regression-oriented test gates are all present. The main evidence-backed gap is release integrity for non-container CLI assets: I found checksum validation for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, but not a repo-observable signature or provenance verification path for those assets themselves. This review is advisory and non-binding; it does not prove security, compliance, certification, endorsement, or SSDF conformance. **Action:** Maintainer should assign this issue to Copilot to add signed or attested verification for CLI release assets and update installer/docs; accept when a release publishes verifiable signatures or provenance for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, `install.sh` or setup paths validate them, and release documentation shows the verification flow. - Critical finding: container release integrity is stronger than CLI release integrity today (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `docs/image-verification.md`, `install.sh`, `docs/releasing.md`). - Critical finding: repository-observable detection and prevention controls are broad and active in source (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`). - Critical metric: 1 promoted backlog item met the threshold for an evidence-backed repository change in this run.
Agent prompt Implement a release-integrity improvement for `github/gh-aw-firewall` focused on SSDF PS.2.1 / PS.3.1 / PS.3.2. Requirements: 1. Extend the release pipeline so `awf-linux-x64`, `awf-linux-arm64`, `awf-darwin-x64`, `awf-darwin-arm64`, `awf-bundle.js`, and `awf.tgz` ship with verifiable signatures or provenance that is generated in CI and published with the release. 2. Update `install.sh` and any setup/install path that currently trusts only `checksums.txt` so it validates the new signature/provenance material before installation, while still failing closed on mismatches. 3. Update release/install docs to show how users verify the CLI assets, parallel to the existing container-image verification guidance. 4. Add or update focused tests that cover failure paths for tampered assets/metadata. 5. Keep existing container signing/SBOM behavior intact. Deliverables: - Workflow changes in `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Installer/setup changes (`install.sh`, `action.yml`, or both as needed) - Documentation updates (`docs/releasing.md`, `README.md`, `docs/image-verification.md` or a better-named CLI verification doc) - Tests proving the verification path fails closed
Assessment metadata, scope, and limitations ### Metadata - Target repository: `github/gh-aw-firewall` - Analyzed commit: `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab` - Target snapshot source: local `target/` checkout plus bounded GitHub metadata reads - Source verification date: `2026-10-13` - Final SSDF baseline used: `NIST SP 800-218 Version 1.1 (final, February 2022)` - Official URLs: - `https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/ssdf` - `https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final` - `https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218` - Machine-readable marker: - `` ### Scope and assumptions - Repository-observable review only: committed files in `target/` and bounded accessible GitHub metadata. - Assessed against the current final SSDF baseline above. The NIST SSDF project page also references `SP 800-218A` as a final SSDF community profile for generative AI and dual-use foundation models, but it augments `SP 800-218` and was **not** treated as a replacement baseline for this repository review. - Findings are risk-based and scoped to evidence visible in this repository snapshot; absence of repository evidence is **not** proof that an organizational control does not exist. ### Inaccessible or non-repository evidence - Branch protection / rulesets details were not readable with the available credential (`gh api repos/github/gh-aw-firewall/branches/main/protection` returned `403 Resource not accessible by personal access token`). - GitHub security feature state, private security alerts, secret-scanning alerts, advisories, internal training records, personnel/process evidence, and private incident-response artifacts were not assessed. - Workflow files provide evidence of intended controls, but this run did not establish historical execution success for every workflow.
PO / PS / PW / RV practice-to-evidence matrix ### Practice matrix | Practice / task focus | Status | Repository-observable evidence | Evidence limits / assumptions | Concrete improvement and risk reduced | |---|---|---|---|---| | `PO.1.1`-`PO.1.3` — define and communicate software-development security requirements | `PARTIAL` | `docs/security.md` defines disclosure expectations; `docs/awf-config-spec.md`, `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, and `docs/image-verification.md` document security-relevant product and release requirements; `README.md` surfaces supported security behaviors. | No visible organization-wide policy register, annual review record, or third-party acquisition/security-contract evidence. | Consolidate repository-scoped secure-release requirements for CLI and container artifacts in one maintained policy/doc so release obligations do not drift. Reduces missed integrity requirements. | | `PO.2.1`-`PO.2.3` — roles, responsibilities, training, leadership commitment | `HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns a maintainer; `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/security.md` define contributor/security reporting paths. | Training, management commitment, and role review cadence are not repository-observable. | Maintain explicit code ownership and review paths; confirm separately whether secure-development roles and training are formalized. Reduces reliance on implicit ownership. | | `PO.3.1`-`PO.3.3` — supporting toolchains and artifacts | `OBSERVED` | `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, and `release.yml` codify automated checks; actions are commit-pinned; release artifacts include `checksums.txt`, `containers.txt`, and schemas. | Runtime hardening and monitoring of hosted CI infrastructure itself are not directly visible. | Preserve pinned-action and artifact-producing workflows; add equivalent provenance coverage for CLI assets. Reduces toolchain tampering blind spots. | | `PO.4.1`-`PO.4.2` — criteria for security checks and protected evidence | `PARTIAL` | High/critical dependency findings fail in `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml`; PR-built container CVEs fail in `supply-chain-scan.yml`; coverage regressions fail in `test-coverage.yml`; CodeQL runs on push/PR/schedule. | Criteria exist across workflows, but I did not find one central repo doc that ties gates, exceptions, and approval criteria together. | Keep machine-enforced thresholds close to the workflows and document exceptions centrally when they are allowed. Reduces inconsistent triage. | | `PO.5.1`-`PO.5.2` — secure development environments and hardened endpoints | `PARTIAL` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, and product docs describe isolated execution, deny-by-default egress, and credential isolation patterns; several workflows use `persist-credentials: false` and least-privilege `permissions`. | Developer endpoint hardening, MFA, runner segmentation, and operational monitoring evidence are mostly outside the repository. | Continue isolating credentials and minimizing runner permissions; verify separately that endpoint and runner hardening matches the documented model. Reduces environment compromise exposure. | | `PS.1.1` — protect code and configuration from unauthorized access/tampering | `PARTIAL` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` exists; workflow actions are SHA-pinned; repository uses GitHub workflow files and code review paths typical for controlled changes. | Repository ACLs, branch protection, and mandatory review enforcement could not be confirmed with the available credential. | Verify rulesets/branch protection separately and keep CODEOWNERS current. Reduces unreviewed change risk. | | `PS.2.1` — provide a mechanism to verify software release integrity | `GAP_FOUND` | `docs/image-verification.md` documents cosign verification for container images. `install.sh` and release docs validate CLI assets with `checksums.txt`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` generates that checksum file, but I did not find repo-observable signatures or provenance verification for `awf-*` binaries or `awf.tgz`. | There could be external verification material not visible here, but none was referenced in repository docs, workflows, or installer paths reviewed. | Publish and validate signed or attested verification material for CLI release assets. Reduces risk that a tampered binary and matching checksum on the same release channel evade detection. | | `PS.3.1`-`PS.3.2` — archive releases and maintain/share provenance | `PARTIAL` | `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes binaries, tarballs, schemas, `checksums.txt`, and `containers.txt`; container images are signed and SBOM-attested; some enclave/cloud-hypervisor artifacts include provenance files. | Equivalent provenance/signature coverage for all CLI assets was not found. Long-term archive controls beyond GitHub Releases are not visible. | Extend provenance/signature publication from selected artifacts to the CLI release set. Reduces incomplete release-forensics coverage. | | `PW.1.1`-`PW.1.3` — design to meet security requirements and mitigate risks | `OBSERVED` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/authentication-architecture.md`, `docs/sandbox-design.md`, and `docs/enclaves-architecture.md` capture security architecture and threat-model reasoning. | This does not prove that every change receives formal threat modeling. | Preserve design docs and keep threat-model updates coupled to security-relevant changes. Reduces design drift. | | `PW.2.1` — independent review of design against security requirements/risk | `PARTIAL` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` supports review; `.github/workflows/security-review.md` exists as a dedicated threat-model/security review workflow; release/process docs contain review-oriented checks. | Could not confirm mandatory execution or independence for every design-affecting change. | Define when security design review is required and link resulting artifacts to changes. Reduces missed design regressions. | | `PW.4.1` / `PW.4.2` / `PW.4.4` — acquire, maintain, and verify reused software/components | `OBSERVED` | `.github/dependabot.yml` updates npm, Docker, and GitHub Actions dependencies; `dependency-audit.yml` and `supply-chain-scan.yml` verify dependency risk; `package-lock.json` and `docs-site/package-lock.json` lock dependencies. | Supplier assurance outside what is codified in repo tooling is not visible. | Keep automated update + audit loops in place and include new ecosystems as they are added. Reduces stale dependency exposure. | | `PW.5.1` — secure coding practices | `OBSERVED` | `package.json` includes `eslint-plugin-security`; source contains dedicated lint/test rules (for example `eslint-rules/no-unsafe-execa.js`); `codeql.yml` enables `security-extended,security-and-quality`. | Secure-coding training and review quality are not directly observable. | Preserve secure-coding automation and add targeted rules when new risk classes emerge. Reduces recurring implementation flaws. | | `PW.6.1`-`PW.6.2` — hardened compilation/interpreter/build configuration | `OBSERVED` | `release.yml` pins actions, signs container images with cosign, generates SBOMs, disables cache for security-critical agent image builds, and runs seccomp verification checks for agent images. | Build-host hardening and provenance for all non-container binaries were not fully visible. | Extend hardened-build outputs with CLI-asset provenance/signatures. Reduces build artifact substitution risk. | | `PW.7.1`-`PW.7.2` — review/analyze human-readable code | `PARTIAL` | `codeql.yml`, ESLint security rules, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and numerous tests provide automated/static review layers. | Mandatory human review enforcement could not be confirmed via rulesets/branch protection. | Keep static analysis current and validate human-review enforcement separately. source_text:
AI Agent: Anthropic thinking block is duplicated across parallel tool calls, Anthropic API rejects the next turn with 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block"
### Bug Description

When an Anthropic Chat Model with thinking enabled (explicitly, or by default on Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.x, which think adaptively when no `thinking` field is sent) returns **one `thinking` block followed by two or more `tool_use` blocks in the same response**, the AI Agent node (Tools Agent V3) fails on the very next model call:

```
400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.1.content.3: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to \"drop_block\". That setting requires the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` value in the `anthropic-beta` header. This request has content before this block that was not present when it was created, first at `messages.1`."}}
```

Surfaced in n8n as `NodeOperationError: Bad request - please check your parameters` on the AI Agent node, thrown from `ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/executeBatch.ts`.

Turns with a single tool call work. The failure only happens when the model issues parallel tool calls, so it is intermittent and depends on the model's choice.

### Root cause (verified in source on master @ 40094e3, 2026-10-15; reproduced on 2.42.7)

The model returns a single assistant turn shaped like `[thinking, tool_use A, tool_use B]`. The thinking block carries a signature that Anthropic binds to that exact turn.

When the agent rebuilds the history after running the tools:

1. `createEngineRequests.ts` → `extractThinkingMetadata()` (line 43) copies the same `thinkingContent` / `thinkingSignature` into the metadata of **every** tool action of the batch. In the saved execution both actions carry an identical `metadata.anthropic.thinkingSignature`.
2. `buildSteps.ts` → `buildSteps()` (line 345) builds the steps. For Gemini it detects parallel calls sharing a thought signature and merges them into one assistant message via `buildSharedGeminiAIMessage()` (lines 288 and 389–412). There is no equivalent branch for Anthropic. Each Anthropic tool call goes through `buildIndividualAIMessage()` (line 236) → `buildAnthropicContentBlocks()` (line 93), which always returns `[thinkingBlock, toolUseBlock]` (line 126).

The history sent on the next call is therefore:

```
Human: ...
AI:   [thinking(sig S), tool_use A]
Tool: result A
AI:   [thinking(sig S), tool_use B]      <- same signature S, replayed under a different prefix
Tool: result B
```

Anthropic now validates that a signed thinking block is replayed under the prefix it was created with. The second copy is preceded by `tool_use A` and `result A`, which did not exist when the signature was minted, so the request is rejected. The comment above the Gemini branch in `buildSteps.ts` describes exactly this problem ("Splitting into separate model turns invalidates the signature"); the Anthropic path simply never got the same handling.

### Related

- #40360 (open) touches the same Anthropic replay path in `buildSteps.ts`.
- #38302 (merged) made empty-text thinking blocks survive the round-trip. This report is the next failure after that fix: the block survives, but it is duplicated.
- #37730 / #37954: explain why thinking is on by default for Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 when Thinking Mode is unset.

### To Reproduce

1. Workflow: Manual Trigger → **AI Agent** (Tools Agent, typeVersion 3.1).
2. Chat model: **Anthropic Chat Model** (typeVersion 1.6), model `claude-opus-5-5` (or `claude-sonnet-5`), **no Thinking Mode option set** (so the model thinks adaptively), or Thinking Mode: Adaptive.
3. Attach two independent tools, e.g. two HTTP Request Tool nodes, or one MCP Client Tool exposing several tools.
4. Prompt with something that invites two lookups at once, e.g. "Look up the user with email X AND search for similar tickets about Y, then summarise."
5. When the model answers with one thinking block and two `tool_use` blocks, both tools run, and the next Anthropic Chat Model call fails with the 400 above. Open the execution → Anthropic Chat Model → second run → input: the history shows `AI: [thinking][tool_use]` twice with the same signature.
6. Prompt it so that it only calls one tool per turn: works.
7. Set Thinking Mode: Disabled, or switch to the OpenAI Chat Model: works.

In my instance this hit 5 production runs in ~24 h on a support-ticket agent with an MCP Client Tool (`get-user` + `find-users`, `get-user` + `get-invoices`, `find-users` + `find-teams`, …). In every failing run, both actions in `subNodeExecutionData.actions[].action.metadata.anthropic` had the identical `thinkingSignature`.

### Expected behavior

Parallel Anthropic tool calls from a single thinking turn should be replayed as **one** assistant message `[thinking, tool_use A, tool_use B]` followed by the tool results, the same way `buildSharedGeminiAIMessage()` already does for Gemini thought signatures. Alternatively, the thinking block should be attached only to the first tool call of the batch and omitted on the others.

### Workarounds

- Set **Thinking Mode: Disabled** on the Anthropic Chat Model node (works since #37954; not possible on models that cannot disable thinking).
- Use a different chat model node.

source_text:
Show HN: Flopper is a hardware explorer for AI infrastructure and beyond
Hello! I built Flopper to make it easier to compare GPUs and understand the tradeoffs for workloads for AI and beyond. When researching GPUs from say Nvidia, AMD, and Huawei, I kept running into the same problem: specs were scattered across datasheets, and matching them to available configurations, vendors, and prices was cumbersome and a bit weird and frankly annoyingggg! AMD made me make an account :( So I started a place to bring that information together. Flopper lets you compare GPU specs, including TDP and compute throughput in terms of flops/tops, alongside estimates for AI workloads or other compute workloads (say, ~FP32 based) I recently added pricing data from dozens of providers to help track how prices change over time. Getting reliable quotes for systems like the NVL72 is still particularly difficult tbh, not sure how I can tell you how much that costs easily due to them being behind large procurement contracts and big multi-nationals. One thing that's become fairlyyyy clear is the interest in consumer cards and local LLMs. The bigger challenge is connecting advertised specs to real-world performance. In our testing so far, I’ve seen roughly 85% of advertised throughput, but that’s a ballpark observation for the workloads I’ve tested, not a general rule and so variable (power, cooling, workload etc). I'm considering a CLI that lets people run benchmarks and submit results, potentially using MLPerf as an automation? That way, we can all compare quoted performance with the workload, configuration etc. I'd love feedback: what information is missing, how can I improve it? And what would you need to see to trust a community-submitted benchmark? Corrections and additions also very welcome - some of the measurements are best efforts (and simple multiplications) but I hope it's of some use. Thanks for looking :)

How Does the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND Flash Memory Work?
NAND flash memory is an essential technology in modern electronic systems, providing non-volatile data storage that retains information even when power is disconnected. It is widely used in embedded systems, automotive electronics, industrial equipment, and digital devices that require reliable memory solutions.
The Micron [MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT](https://globx.eu/products/micron/mt29f1g08abafah4-aatf) NAND Flash Memory is a 1Gb single-level cell (SLC) NAND flash memory device designed for applications that need dependable data storage and parallel memory access. With an 8-bit data bus, a 3.3V I/O interface, and an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C, it is suited to demanding embedded and automotive environments.
Understanding how this NAND flash memory works helps engineers select appropriate storage components for electronic system design, firmware storage, and industrial applications.

**What Is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?**
The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT is a non-volatile [NAND flash memory](https://doodleordie.com/profile/globxoffical) component manufactured by Micron Technology. It stores digital information in memory cells that retain their programmed state without continuous electrical power.
The device provides a 1-gigabit storage capacity, organized as 128M × 8 bits. Its parallel interface allows a compatible processor or memory controller to transfer data through an eight-bit bus.
Unlike volatile memory such as SRAM and DRAM, NAND flash memory preserves stored information when the system shuts down. This makes it useful for storing firmware, configuration data, and other information required when an electronic device starts operating.

**How Does NAND Flash Memory Work?**
NAND flash memory stores information by controlling the electrical charge within specialized semiconductor memory cells. These cells represent digital data through different electrical states.

The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT uses single-level cell technology, meaning each memory cell stores one bit of information.
Its operation can be understood through three main processes.

1. Storing Data in Memory Cells
During programming, the memory device applies controlled electrical conditions to place charge into the storage structure of selected memory cells. The resulting electrical characteristics represent the programmed data.
In SLC NAND flash, each cell represents either a logical 0 or a logical 1. Because each cell stores one bit, SLC technology offers a straightforward storage arrangement compared with multi-level NAND technologies.
This design is useful in embedded applications where predictable memory behavior and endurance are important considerations.

2. Reading Stored Information
When a processor needs information, it sends the appropriate command and address to the NAND flash memory. The device accesses the selected location and determines the stored bit values by sensing the electrical characteristics of the memory cells.
The retrieved data is transferred through the eight-bit parallel interface.
A compatible controller or processor coordinates the read operation and uses the returned information for tasks such as loading firmware, accessing configuration settings, or retrieving stored program data.

3. Erasing and Reprogramming Data
NAND flash memory generally erases data in blocks rather than allowing arbitrary individual bytes to be overwritten directly.
When existing information must be replaced, the system typically erases the relevant block before programming new data into it. Pages are used for read and program operations, while blocks contain multiple pages.
The controller or firmware must manage these operations correctly, including handling bad blocks and monitoring data integrity where required.

**What Makes SLC NAND Flash Different?**
Single-level cell NAND flash stores one bit per memory cell. Other NAND technologies, including MLC, TLC, and QLC, store multiple bits per cell.
The main difference is how many electrical states each cell must distinguish.
SLC NAND uses two principal states, making the interpretation of stored data simpler than in technologies that use more states per cell. SLC memory is therefore often selected for applications that prioritize endurance, reliable operation, and consistent embedded storage behavior.
However, actual performance and endurance depend on the device specifications, operating conditions, and the system's memory management strategy.

**Applications of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
The combination of SLC NAND technology, parallel access, and an extended operating temperature range makes this memory component relevant to several types of electronic systems.

**Automotive Electronics**
Automotive electronic control units may need non-volatile storage for firmware, calibration information, and configuration data. A memory device rated for operation from -40°C to +105°C can be considered for suitable automotive designs, provided all electrical, qualification, and reliability requirements are satisfied.

**Industrial Embedded Systems**
Industrial controllers, monitoring equipment, and automation systems often need persistent storage for program code and system settings. NAND flash memory can provide this storage without requiring continuous power.

**Firmware and Boot Storage**
Embedded platforms can use NAND flash to store firmware images and other startup information. The processor or bootloader must support the memory interface and the device's command and timing requirements.

**Communication and Control Equipment**
Networking devices, industrial communication modules, and electronic control products may use parallel NAND memory for firmware and data storage. The suitability of this specific device depends on capacity requirements, controller compatibility, and the application's reliability targets.

**Advantages of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
Several characteristics make this component worth considering during embedded memory selection.

**Non-volatile storage**: Stored information remains available when the power supply is disconnected.
SLC memory architecture: One bit per cell provides a simpler storage scheme and is commonly associated with higher write endurance than higher-density multi-bit NAND technologies.

**Parallel data interface:** The eight-bit bus supports data transfer to compatible memory controllers and processors.
Extended temperature range: The specified -40°C to +105°C operating range supports designs exposed to a broad range of environmental temperatures.

**Compact package:** The 63-ball VFBGA package helps integrate memory into space-constrained electronic designs.
These benefits must be evaluated alongside the full datasheet, system architecture, and application-specific requirements.

Third, consider bad-block management, wear management, data retention, and power-loss behavior. These factors are particularly important in products that store firmware or frequently update persistent information.

Finally, confirm the package footprint, voltage limits, environmental requirements, and the exact ordering suffix. Components with similar part numbers may have different package, temperature, or electrical characteristics.

Owner confirmed ShinaCare must account for **COD, Visa/Mastercard and Vodafone Cash**, not assume COD is the only future checkout payment method. **C1 backend exit remains a REAL COD Cart-to-Cash E2E**, PLUS a tested lean payment-method-aware core/guardrails under [GLO-241](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-241>). For online methods keep unverified attempts PENDING, never synthesize paid/cash/settled, and avoid creating COD driver obligations. Separate provider settlement/payout from payment confirmation. Actual provider integration requires explicit owner approval and remains a later milestone.

---

BACKEND ONLY. Demonstrate one persisted Cart→quote→COD order→durable sourcing→consolidated supplier PO/confirmed allocations→Hub receipt→barcode-verified preparation+packing documents→driver run/custody/delivery→door-cash declaration→physical cash count→single correct settlement. Include availability/return/refund/support and supplier payables. No Storefront/Business Workspace design or implementation in this phase.

This is an **acceptance gate, not duplicate implementation**; work in linked existing canonical W issues and any verified missing backend task. Existing C0 cross-workspace UI acceptance (AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#118) is explicitly deferred, NOT Done.

## Required reproducible test evidence (same identifiers throughout)

- [ ] Real PostgreSQL test DB (\*\_test), migrations, scoped actor accounts for customer/guest/admin/supplier/hub/driver/cashier; no Neon/shared/production DB.
- [ ] Server-only cart quantity/revision, catalog sellability/prices, authoritative quote, price-change 409/requote, idempotent COD order, persisted confirmed address + geo pin, Cairo/Giza serviceability and role-safe pin access.
- [ ] Durable order.placed handoff/recovery, idempotent supply plan; supplier+SKU aggregated PO with N:1 quantity-aware PO-line-to-allocation mapping and deterministic partial/fallback; no late duplicate supply.
- [ ] Real Hub receiving quantity vs supplier Ready, correct source links, scan mismatch blocked, packed unique shipment identity and printable thermal receipt/slip data (physical printer testing deferred).
- [ ] Driver-only assigned manifests with secured coordinates/stop ordering, handoff scanning, dispatch atomic order+shipment effects, delivered/failed/retry/return consistency and safe replay.
- [ ] Expected COD vs declared door cash vs counted cashier cash vs settled; driver/courier/hub scope; zero duplicate/failed/undelivered settlement; explicit short/over variance; exact Decimal arithmetic.
- [ ] Supplier payable based on correct received/approved qty/cost snapshot, EGP, race-safe idempotency; cancellation/refund/manual COD refund evidence, support escalation and event/outbox truthfulness.
- [ ] Query/read APIs for role-scoped operational inboxes (no UI), RBAC/IDOR/PII negative HTTP cases, concurrency/transaction failure recovery.
- [ ] Single full-backend C2C automated integration suite, including critical negative cases; exact Git SHA, commands, passed/failed/skipped counts, DB target; no simulated success evidence.

Backend PASS requires one replayable HTTP/API→DB run from cart to settled money, accurate cross-domain state, and documented negative/authorization/concurrency tests. Manual physical cash, printer, real supplier and all role UI acceptance are separate later operational gates; do NOT misrepresent them as backend-proven. Keep this issue In Progress until all backend bullets pass. No fixed date.

## Execution guardrails

Reuse implemented modules (do not rewrite Cart/Quote/Shipping/Scan/Settlement blindly); inspect HEAD, staged 26 deletions and private uploads before touching code; never broad-stage/reset; one coding agent at a time; scoped commits; no merge without owner approval. Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

WPF XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content, enabling remote code execution after user interaction.
