source_text:
[Design proposal] Prospect Intelligence — store audits, business contacts & sales handoff
# Design proposal — CartShift Prospect Intelligence (review requested)

**Status:** proposed architecture, **not approved for implementation**. No automated prospect messages, scans, data imports, or deployments are authorized by this issue.  
**Business context:** support a 30-day €5,000 collections objective; prioritize a revenue-producing pilot over a large engineering project.  
**Owner:** CartShift Studio. **Primary operator:** sales manager (Adi), with technical approval by founder.

## 1. Problem & outcomes

Today CartShift has: (a) a public Store Analyzer, (b) inbound marketing leads in `marketing_leads`, (c) agency/client portal and proposals, and (d) an existing manually researched prospect spreadsheet (14 Israeli candidates as of 2026-10-08). It does **not** have a distinct, evidence-backed *outbound prospect* workflow with business-contact discovery and channel-eligibility controls. Asking a nontechnical sales manager to diagnose Liquid/UX issues before selling is a bottleneck.

**Desired operator journey:** import/enter store → lightweight public-domain audit → evidence review → identify suitable business role/public contact → legal/consent review → hand off to Adi → discovery → founder-approved scoped proposal → won/lost/paid attribution.

**Success measures for pilot (targets, not projections):** 20–30 *consented/manual approved-for-scan* Israeli business domains; 5–8 meaningful verified findings; ≥5 leads with a valid next action; 3 discovery conversations; 1 scoped proposal. Track actual consent/channel review and cash collected, not just scan counts.

## 2. Findings in current repo (main as inspected 2026-10-14)

- Public scan orchestration: `lib/services/analyzer.ts`, `lib/services/scraper.ts`, `lib/utils/safe-store-fetch.ts`, `app/api/analyze-store/route.ts` (120s maxDuration).
- Existing inbound/self-submitted marketing: `lib/services/portal-marketing.ts`, `lib/services/store-analysis-leads.ts`, `app/[locale]/portal/agency/leads/MarketingLeadsClient.tsx`, `marketing_leads` and `marketing_email_jobs`.
- Agency authorization: `lib/auth/server-agency.ts`, `lib/utils/permissions.ts`, `firestore.rules`; `sales_manager` already exists.
- CRM/client handoff: `lib/types/portal.ts` (Organization has CRM contact fields), `portal_organizations`; agency proposals/requests already exist.
- React Query hooks in `lib/hooks`; localization sources `messages/src/en/...` and `messages/src/he/...`; never edit generated translations.

**Architectural constraint:** do not put researched companies into `marketing_leads`: this collection has an email requirement, inbound attribution/consent semantics, existing email jobs, and its scoring does not represent buying intent. Do not auto-create portal clients or invitations while prospecting.

## 3. Options & decision proposal

A. Spreadsheet + manual audit, no product work: cheapest/faster, poor process visibility.  
B. **Recommended:** thin, separate `agency_prospects` domain inside existing Agency Portal; reuse approved analyzer primitives and proposals; human-reviewed business-contact workflow. Best incremental value/cost.  
C. New autonomous crawler + contact enrichment + mass outreach: expensive, harder to audit, greater legal/privacy risk. **Defer**.

Ship B in vertical slices with A as the first-week pilot fallback. No new paid enrichment subscriptions, recurring scan scheduler, or new CRM service in MVP.

## 4. UX / roles

- New Agency Portal route `/[locale]/portal/agency/prospects` with list (status, brand, issue confidence, source, owner, last verified, next action), filters, and detail page.
- Prospect detail tabs: **Overview**, **Findings & Evidence**, **Business Contacts**, **Activity & Compliance**. Prominent empty/unknown evidence states; no fabricated impact estimates.
- Adi (`sales_manager`): read and triage, add discovery notes, select business-contact path, request technical review, update sales activity. May draft but not send unsolicited messages via app.
- Founder (`owner/admin`): approve finding, technical feasibility, estimate, proposal, relationship status, contact-channel eligibility/legal basis, suppression override policy. Suppression **cannot** be overridden into an automatic send.
- Client users have **zero** access. Agency developers/viewers have no access by default; explicitly grant roles only if needed.
- On qualification, link to existing proposal/agency-client workflow; do not duplicate proposal/payment logic. Conversion must preserve `prospectId` provenance.

## 5. Proposed data model (Firestore, non-public)

`agency_prospects/{prospectId}`
```ts
type ProspectStage = 'new'|'needs_review'|'qualified'|'contact_research'|'contact_ready'|'in_conversation'|'proposal'|'won'|'lost'|'suppressed';
type OutreachEligibility = 'unknown'|'review_required'|'consent_recorded'|'existing_relationship'|'approved_partner_channel'|'blocked';
type Prospect = {
  id: string; canonicalDomain: string; storeUrl: string; brandName: string;
  country: 'IL'; platform: 'shopify'|'other'|'unknown'; platformConfidence: 'verified'|'likely'|'unknown';
  sourceType: 'manual'|'spreadsheet_import'|'referral'; sourceReference?: string;
  stage: ProspectStage; ownerUid?: string; linkedOrgId?: string; linkedRequestId?: string;
  outreachEligibility: OutreachEligibility; eligibilityReviewedBy?: string; eligibilityReviewedAt?: Timestamp;
  permissionEvidenceUrl?: string; permissionNote?: string; doNotContact: boolean;
  nextAction?: string; nextActionAt?: Timestamp; fitScore?: number; fitReason?: string;
  lastAuditedAt?: Timestamp; lastVerifiedAt?: Timestamp;
  createdBy: string; createdAt: Timestamp; updatedAt: Timestamp;
}
```
Subcollections:
- `findings/{findingId}`: code/category, severity, business relevance, `observedUrl`, text excerpt/screenshot reference, observation time, `evidenceType` (`html`/`visual`/`manual`), `confidence`, `verificationStatus` (`unverified`/`verified`/`rejected`/`stale`), reviewer/time. Never claim hidden HTML is user-visible without screenshot confirmation.
- `contacts/{contactId}`: `name?`, `role?`, `businessEmail?`, `professionalProfileUrl?`, `officialContactUrl?`, `sourceUrl`, `observedAt`, `confidence`, `isPersonalData`, `verifiedBy?`, `verifiedAt?`, `contactStatus` (candidate/verified/invalid/deletion_requested). Never generate/guess addresses, scrape personal phone numbers, or conflate publication with permission.
- `activities/{activityId}`: timestamp, actorUid, type, notes, old/new stage, linked proposal, recorded consent/source. Append-only through authenticated API.

Separate optional `agency_prospect_scan_runs/{scanId}`: prospectId, requestedBy, start/end, safe bounded config, status, page counts, refusal/error codes, cost counters; no full HTML or sensitive cookies retained.

Identity: use deterministic normalized domain ID for first import (after validating actual canonical merchant domain); maintain aliases for verified `myshopify.com` names; upsert idempotently and avoid duplicate client/prospect records. Existing inbound lead with same domain produces a suggested manual match — do not merge consent/state automatically.

## 6. Scan & business contact discovery

**MVP is explicitly manual/on-demand**, not an autonomous internet crawler.

1. Operator supplies an approved domain or bounded CSV. Preflight domain/URL, publicly visible Shopify signals, robots.txt and website terms. Disallowed or uncertain pages are skipped and flagged.
2. Server-side fetch **only** public pages; default cap 6 pages/site (homepage, 1 collection, 1 product, About, Contact, Team if available); throttle ≤1 req/2 seconds/host, no concurrent scans for one host, timeouts, max body size and audit rate quotas. No checkout submission, password entry, form submission, hidden endpoints, robots bypass, captcha bypass or authenticated pages.
3. Reuse analyzer functions selectively; avoid invoking full Lighthouse/Puppeteer for each store by default. Extract deterministic issues first: clearly missing translation keys, broken internal links, inconsistent policies, content-type mismatches, visible CTA accessibility candidates. Some findings require separate visual confirmation. Store concise evidence + timestamps only. No unsupported 'revenue loss' claims.
4. Contact discovery from the site's public About/Team/Contact pages, explicit business-schema entries and **official** partner/supplier channels. Identify buying role rather than insist on a named person. Do not crawl LinkedIn profiles or use email-pattern guessing. Record source and verification date.
5. Require human confirmation of relevance, facts, fit, contact and eligibility before queueing to Adi.
6. Flag old evidence stale after 14 days until reverified. For pilot, auto-removal/minimization review after 90 days for stale findings; personal contact records require a documented retention period and deletion flow. Suppression records retain only the minimum needed to prevent re-contact.

**Security:** current `safe-store-fetch.ts` checks host DNS and manual redirects but is not by itself a fully hardened crawler permission/sandbox system. Before any multi-page operation, cover DNS rebinding, alternate IP encodings, IPv4-mapped IPv6, redirects to internal hosts, metadata endpoints, deceptive ports, public suffix canonicalization, max response bytes and pinned network resolution / controlled egress. Add explicit robots policy checks and no untrusted HTML → prompt-instruction execution. No unreviewed third-party AI processing of personal contact fields.

## 7. Contact legality and outreach policy

- Separate **contact discoverability** from **permission to market**. A published business email/contact form is not opt-in.
- Default `review_required` / `unknown`; only human authorized reviewer may change eligibility with evidence; `blocked` and opt-outs win.
- Israel's Communications Law §30A generally requires prior consent for promotional email/SMS; a narrowly defined one-time business request for consent is **not** blanket permission to pitch. Contact forms are not an automatic loophole.
- Check GDPR/German controller obligations and Israeli privacy rules where applicable; legal review needed before any outbound workflow.
- Product MVP provides contact details, manual next action and copyable **internal research brief** — **no Send button, mailto campaign, contact-form automation, enrichment credits or bulk outreach**. Future send functionality is an independent gated project after legal sign-off, explicit consent records, unsubscribe/suppression enforcement and tests.
- Sources: Israel §30A legislative text https://knesset-tracker.co.il/knesset/statute/2000002 ; Israeli Privacy Protection Authority amendment-13 Q&A https://www.gov.il/he/pages/tikun13_qa?chapterIndex=6 .

## 8. API & security contract

Proposed authenticated routes, all server-side validated Zod, explicit role/field allowlists, audit log, pagination:
- `GET/POST /api/portal/agency/prospects` list/create or import preview.
- `GET/PATCH /api/portal/agency/prospects/[prospectId]` details, allowed stage/owner/next-action changes.
- `POST /api/portal/agency/prospects/[prospectId]/scan` manual, bounded, idempotent; **never** send outreach.
- `POST /api/portal/agency/prospects/[prospectId]/review` founder technical/contact eligibility decisions.
- `POST /api/portal/agency/prospects/[prospectId]/activities` append-only notes/events.
- `POST /api/portal/agency/prospects/import/preview` validate/dedupe before confirmed import.

Firestore rules: deny all client access; deny direct client writes for server-owned prospect collections and subcollections; use `requireAgencySession` with **explicit** owner/admin/sales-manager operation checks in server code (existing helper is broad), and rate limits. Ensure server request is not authorized by client-provided ownerUid or agencyRole. Index `stage, ownerUid, nextActionAt`, `canonicalDomain` / `updatedAt` only as queries need. Sensitive data never exposed in public routes or telemetry.

## 9. Implementation slices (each releasable)

**P0 — revenue-first, 1–2 developer days target:** add private prospect data model, manual create/import preview from existing spreadsheet, dedupe, triage list & detail, source/verification flags, owner/next action. Do not scan automatically. Adi can use it immediately; alternatively work from existing Google Sheet until P0 ships.

**P1 — bounded shop audit:** one manually triggered safe crawl per prospect; deterministic evidence with confidence, reviewer status, cheap per-site limits, skipped/error states; tests for SSRF/robots. No PageSpeed by default.

**P2 — business-contact research:** retrieve only official/public company contact/role clues from allowed pages; provenance + confidence; manual confirmation, channel-eligibility + suppression; never send automatically.

**P3 — sales-to-revenue handoff:** activity timeline, reminder date, `sales_manager` work queue, role-safe founder technical review, links to existing proposal/request/paid revenue; basic funnel metrics per source. Conversion does not imply cash collected.

**P4 (after pilot metrics):** scheduled scans, optional AI-assisted issue summarization, external enrichment integrations or deeper visual snapshots — separately justified by performance, compliance and budget; none in MVP.

## 10. Acceptance / security tests

- Import the existing 14-company research sheet to **preview**, manually approve records, normalize duplicate domains, preserve original evidence URLs and 2026-10-08 observation dates, **no scan or outreach** on import.
- Unknown Shopify identification stays `unknown`; non-Shopify candidates not inaccurately tagged Shopify.
- Unsupported/hidden DOM text is never displayed as verified customer-visible issue.
- Disallowed robots/host/redirects and internal addresses are blocked even after redirect/DNS transition.
- One domain cannot trigger duplicate simultaneous scans; quotas/timeouts/errors are user-visible without crashing the queue.
- Discovery never generates an email address; a role-only contact is acceptable.
- All contacts require source URLs, dates, and privacy-aware retention/deletion.
- Public or client auth cannot read or mutate prospect contacts/findings; sales_manager cannot approve technical scope or change legal gate; unauthorized reviewer actions 403.
- Suppressed prospect cannot transition to contact-ready; no send/marketing job is created by any scan/import.
- Existing inbound marketing dashboard, analyzer, client roles and proposal/payment flows remain unchanged.
- Hebrew RTL + English translation coverage; desktop/mobile and keyboard QA.
- Unit tests (Vitest), route auth tests, Firestore emulator rules, dry-run fixture scan. **No CI reruns or Vercel preview deployments during planning.**

## 11. Review questions / decisions before writing product code

1. Confirm **Adi as sales_manager** (rather than broader agency admin) and founder-only approval of technical + contact eligibility gates.
2. Confirm initial **Israel-only, Shopify-first, manual import + on-demand scans**; no bulk prospect messaging.
3. Agree to a **14-day commercial pilot** before any heavy automation; track real conversations and cash results.
4. Legal reviewer determines if/how business-consent requests can lawfully be conducted; engineering must not infer permission.

**Deliverable of this issue:** reviewable architecture + milestone plan. Once approved, write a repository spec in `docs/superpowers/specs/` and a test-first implementation plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/` before code changes.

Show HN: Merlin, Run Your Claude Code and Codex from Slack, Linear and GitHub
Hi HN, I built Merlin to let you use your own Claude Code and Codex subscription from Slack, Linear, and GitHub. There is a desktop app for macOS and Windows, and a CLI daemon for Linux. When someone mentions Merlin in a Slack thread or Linear issue comment, the task runs on that team member's machine, using their own Claude Code or Codex runtime, and progress and results come back to the original thread. Teammates can steer the agent mid-run. Merlin also has schedules, shared skills, and memory. I know you've probably heard about Claude Tag. Merlin is similar to that but also different. The model usage goes to the Claude Code or Codex subscription instead of API bill, and you can use Merlin across different surfaces to streamline workflow instead of just in Slack (Linear's agent session works particularly well with Merlin. You can just leverage Linear as your control panel for agentic work using Merlin). Merlin also runs on your local machines, which means that you can use your local context including MCPs, skills and local files instead of in a cloud sandbox. Merlin does not upload your working directory, and provider credentials stay on the device. The request and the context it needs pass through Merlin. Runtimes start private, and an owner can make one public so teammates, including non-engineers, can use it. But there're also some limits, and we'll probably deal with them in future updates:
- An offline or sleeping machine can't take work. The same issue as OpenClaw. But if you have a mac mini or ec2 setup it should be fine.
- Linux is CLI only. We may later add desktop for Linux.
- While runtime delegation isn't a problem for now, we're still working on how to make the best use of each team member's local runtime and let them work together cohesively. We've been internally using Merlin for quite some time. It really helps when you're trying to add some AI juice to the conversation or just delegate things to your agents. I think it reduces the friction of having to do the copying & pasting and switch to another app to ask for AI's input when you're having a discussion in a collaborative environment like Slack or Linear. It's really the fastest way from intent to execution. Pricing: free for up to 5 active users and 1,000 requests/month. We think this should get small teams started and get real value from it. Team is $59/mo and Scale is $99/mo, with a 14-day Team trial and no credit card required. I'm here all day to answer questions, and I'd especially like to hear whether non-engineers on your team would actually use this.

We still do code review but it does bottleneck how much we can ship. I'm looking at what we can do to alleviate this. Here's what I think the near fut
We still do code review but it does bottleneck how much we can ship. I'm looking at what we can do to alleviate this. Here's what I think the near future may look like, as far as getting more value per time spent out of human code review. I'm coming at this from the POV of an org that still mandates human code review and I think a lot of this advice doesn't hold if you are all-in on the black box software factory approach. If you're reviewing code you're responsible for, your job now is to provide stewardship of its long term technical direction even if you are not personally reading and writing every line of code. This means preserving the coherence of designs past and present, and ensuring that they are not being worked around in service of a short-term goal. Stop reading every line of every file to look for minor gotchas. Focus on core business logic and whether invariants are modeled well & to the fullest extent possible by the type system. Agents are better than most humans now at spotting insane gotchas. At least one frontier model should review most PRs. In the before times, you could argue that TODO comments and small nits on PRs should be addressed, because most likely they'd never get attention again once the PR merges. Now, small issues should instead be automatically recorded and followed up on quickly by another agent. Minor code quality issues should become rules, and old code should be constantly revisited by agents to bring it up to par with new code. Provide the transcripts of the session with the PR. Look for evidence of thoughtful direction & solid premise behind the conversation that led to the PR being made. In addition to providing more mentorship opportunities to the author, this also discourages meat proxying/low-value-added uses of AI. Asking someone to rewrite or completely discard a PR that's just a bad idea should no longer be the ego bruising event it once was (at least with respect to the cost sunk to make the PR). Require a higher bar for proving that code works and stays working. The testing pyramid IMO should now be more of a testing hourglass. Or an upside-down pyramid, even. Automated E2E tests should be abundant. Every feature should receive adequate manual testing by an agent, with proof of work. In the vein of "stays working," look for good observability and guardrails around a feature. If you're doing a good job of leveraging agents to keep code up to par, this means adding (and cycling out) feature flags, ensuring that there's adequate logging, having a cohesive monitoring solution with good coverage, and a plan for what to do if there's an issue in prod.

For every autonomous Matrix worker, including Librarians, **65% of the worker's evaluated performance/KPI** measures attributable contribution toward verified money-in or the evidenced removal of a real blocker on that path. This is a performance-accountability weight, **not a 65% wall-clock, time, compute, staffing, activity, or blanket sales quota**. It does not expand a worker's mandate or transfer ownership. Contribution must be attributable, observable, and evidence-backed.

## 2. Outcome truth

Keep these states separate:
- **Verified money-in:** received/withdrawable funds or settlement independently verified.
- **Lifecycle progress:** qualified response, accepted work, contract, invoice/receivable, submission/award, delivery acceptance, or another source-backed state change.

source_text:
MED-PRICE-001: build quality-gated global medicine affordability and procurement model
## Goal

Design and prototype an open, auditable decision-support system that helps participating health systems obtain essential medicines at the **lowest sustainable, quality-assured landed cost** while improving reliable availability and equitable access.

The objective is not to optimize purchase price alone. A low unit price that creates stockouts, short shelf life, unsafe product quality, concentrated supply, expensive distribution, or unaffordable patient co-payments is not a good outcome.

## Why this matters

WHO says essential medicines should be available at all times, affordable to people and health systems, and of assured quality; the 2025 WHO Model List contains over 520 medicines, including 374 for children:
https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/B09474

Proven mechanisms already exist:
- WHO recommends quality-assured generics/biosimilars, price transparency, tendering and pooled procurement among the policy tools countries can combine: https://www.who.int/teams/health-product-and-policy-standards/medicines-selection-ip-and-affordability/affordability-pricing
- The Global Fund's Pooled Procurement Mechanism managed about US$1.02 billion in orders for implementers in 81 countries during 2025: https://www.theglobalfund.org/en/sourcing-management/procurement-tools/
- UNICEF publishes multiyear-agreement antimalarial price data: https://www.unicef.org/supply/documents/antimalarials-price-data
- The Medicines Patent Pool tracks licensed product access, registrations and supply readiness: https://medicinespatentpool.org/accesspal
- South Africa's National Department of Health publishes a medicine-price database including Single Exit Prices and logistics fees: https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-pee/
- WHO prequalification provides a quality benchmark for products eligible for its programme: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/prequalification-of-medicines-by-who

## V1 scope

Start with an offline, synthetic-data-first procurement simulator for a small set of essential generic medicines; do not ingest patient-level data.

### Required data contracts

1. **Medicine presentation identity:** INN/active ingredient, strength, dosage form, route, package size, target FHIR/ATC/other coding systems only where correctly mapped, country/jurisdiction, registration status, and licensed market scope.
2. **Price observation:** currency, observation date, unit basis, public/private or tender channel, supplier, price type (ex-manufacturer/SEP/tender/landed), contract duration, volume tier, tax/duty/logistics inclusion, source locator, exact capture digest and source-specific licensing/reuse status.
3. **Quality/admission evidence:** regulator registration and status, WHO prequalification or an accepted stringent/regional/national approval criterion for the intended procurement channel, GMP/quality-system evidence, product identity and strength match, recall/alert state, and expiry/shelf-life conditions.
4. **Supply offer:** supplier and manufacturing site, offered volume, production capacity evidence, lead time, delivery reliability evidence, minimum order, shelf life at delivery, temperature/cold-chain needs, API/key starting material dependencies when known, and contract terms.
5. **Demand scenario:** aggregate demand by period and geography, uncertainty range, seasonality, service-level target, current stock, lead-time demand, and shortage/expiry costs. Use synthetic aggregates until lawful and governed operational data is separately qualified.
6. **Decision/award record:** input-manifest and policy digests, eligibility gates, scenario assumptions, candidate offers, selected allocation, dissent/counter-evidence, conflicts of interest, reviewer approval, and reasons for excluding offers.

Keep raw patient or beneficiary identifiers out of public artifacts and procurement receipts.

## Optimization objective

Minimize total expected lifecycle cost, not just quoted price:

`expected_total_cost = acquisition + freight + insurance + duties/tax + quality testing + storage/cold-chain + financing + expiry/wastage + shortage/stockout impact`

Subject to hard constraints for lawful market access, product quality, approved/authorized use, capacity, lead time, available budget, shelf life, and required service level. Also constrain supplier concentration and maintain minimum resilience (e.g. qualified second source or safety stock) where supply risk justifies it. The model may display trade-offs but cannot relax safety or quality gates to achieve a lower score.

Fairness requirements: report price and availability separately by country/channel and date; distinguish absolute price from affordability relative to local public-health budgets and household burden; model tiered prices and cross-subsidies transparently; do not infer willingness to pay from sensitive individual data or use identity/reputation scores to allocate medicines.

## Mechanisms to compare

- pooled/regional procurement and standardized tender lots;
- multi-winner tenders and volume commitments that preserve qualified backup suppliers;
- quality-assured generic and biosimilar uptake;
- transparent price comparisons and lifecycle cost-plus analysis;
- patent-pool/voluntary licence and regulatory-registration availability mapping;
- demand pooling, forecasting, order consolidation and inventory optimization;
- regional manufacturing/technology transfer when scale, quality systems and delivered total cost support it;
- public R&D and purchasing agreements with access and transparency conditions;
- packaging, formulation, distribution and cold-chain efficiency;
- appropriate tax/markup and patient co-payment policy scenarios.

No claim that all interventions lower prices in every context: the simulator must show assumptions, uncertainty, market concentration and failure modes.

## Luminous stack integration

- **Mycelix:** authoritative provenance/snapshot/selector references, licence and eligibility evidence, supplier/contract decision receipts and correction history. No universal trust score.
- **Symthaea:** demand forecasting, scenario analysis, sensitivity/uncertainty and counterfactual ranking against simple baselines. Advisory only.
- **Sol-Atlas:** map and timeline of price observations, registrations, licence territory, shortage risk, evidence gaps and scenario results. Visualization confers no authority.
- **Mycelix-Health:** medicine presentation / procurement domain contracts, quality gates, safety/recall integrations and qualified human award workflow.
- **Nix/CI:** pinned toolchains, immutable public synthetic corpus, reproducible scenario manifests and exact-head results.

Do not mix clinical efficacy/safety evidence, medicine registration, supply eligibility, tender eligibility, price observation and contract award into one Boolean or reputation score. Each requires a separate state and source.

## Required adversarial tests

- Same presentation but different strength/form/pack cannot compare as the same unit.
- Same named price with different unit basis, currency, observation date, tender channel or included logistics is not directly comparable without explicit normalization.
- Missing/unknown licence territory or registration does not become eligible.
- Low-price offer fails hard quality gate -> never wins.
- Price-only winner causes high stockout risk -> report total-cost/resilience trade-off and eligible alternatives.
- Single supplier concentration breaches policy -> infeasible or explicit exception with accountable human approval.
- Stale price/recall/registration evidence -> Indeterminate/review-needed.
- No offer or missing price data never appears as “free” or a successful procurement.
- Different FX rates / freight / expiry assumptions produce a traceable changed scenario.
- Unsupported data licence means no unlicensed redistribution; metadata-only evidence remains metadata-only.
- Model's selected offer is not itself a contract, purchase order or payment instruction.
- Simulated savings cannot be represented as realized/clinical outcomes.

## Deliverables and acceptance

1. Versioned Rust input/output types and synthetic dataset.
2. Deterministic baseline for eligible-offer filtering and cost normalization.
3. Small exact/transparent allocation optimizer with budget, service-level and concentration constraints; compare against lowest-price-only baseline.
4. Scenario report for purchase price, landed cost, service level, expiry, supplier concentration, uncertainty and access/affordability by geography.
5. Independent checker recomputes eligibility and cost from immutable inputs, separate from the optimizer.
6. Tests and replay receipt demonstrate deterministic output for the same input manifest/policy.
7. No purchase/execution authority; final award stays with an accountable buyer under local law and procurement rules.

## Initial demonstration

Use synthetic offers for 10–20 generic essential-medicine presentations across 3–5 hypothetical regions. Then adapt public price observations from WHO/UNICEF/Global Fund/South African NDoH only when the exact source, date, unit, licence and comparability conditions are recorded.

## Non-goals

- No unsupervised procurement, prescribing, therapeutic substitution, or patient-level allocation.
- No bypassing patents, marketing authorization, import controls, GMP, pharmacovigilance or procurement law.
- No treating WHO prequalification as automatic legal authorization in every country.
- No claim of realized savings or patient outcomes from a simulator.
- No assumption that local manufacturing is always cheaper than pooled imports.

ASK: HN Help and Forward Advice, Ideas: New Lossless cmpr MRT/CT, Astro
Hey HN, at first, i'm not from that subject field so I dont know what to do. I'm an ordinary engeneer with basics and unorthodox thinking. I used Claude to help me implement. Its a process of several months and bazills of millions of tokens of work. I can't show or disclose, begging for your understanding. I can't beat WEBP lossless on kodak test suite, YET; But I'm like 5% worser on RGBa. CMYK's similar. Here, the advantage is me being 5-15x faster as WEBP / other lossless codecs. Not yet fully confirmed, but promissing results WEBP will be knocked too. My lossy compression is better than JPEG sometimes, but always ~10++ times faster. Very big building field right now. The figures are very promissing on lossless video. On cpu cycles beating every SOTA methods by being upto 15x faster or so. Possible path. My lossy shows better sharpness and details in (very) fast moving scenes (1080p, 2k, 4k incl. hdr), while being only ~5-10% bigger than heif and avc, and others with comperable compression params. It seems to scale res/depth without issues. Runs on data from various MRT/CT Imagers and formats found for download show ~15%-50% percent better compression as SOTA/DICOM, at a fraction of cycles. source_text:
If-node in sub-workflow causes properties of previous node to become not found when all items go the false path
### Bug Description

The properties of an earlier node can become not found. This Problem occurs when between the node that sets the property and the node that tries to access it there is a sub-workflow and inside that sub-workflow there is an if-node and all items inside the sub-workflow will go the false path of the if-node.

The error does not occur if all items of the sub-workflow will go the true path or if some items go true and others go false.

Also the property seems to be not found if the expression uses "item" to reference a previous node. When using "first()" or "all()[0]" it seems to work.

Maybe related: When debugging an execution where all items in an if-node use the false path and a merge node is behind it, the merge node is unable to execute.

### To Reproduce

[main-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341808/main-workflow.json)
[sub-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341809/sub-workflow.json)

These json files show a main-workflow and a sub-workflow to reproduce this issue. 
If the value properties of all items in the "Set Array Data" nodes myItems field  is true, the workflow works. But if all are set to false the code node at the end will throw an error and in the edit fiels node at the end you can see the difference between the expressions.

### Expected behavior

After the described sub-workflow, nodes should still be able to access earlier nodes via the " $('NameOfEarlyNode').item.json " expression, even if all items used the false path in the subworkflow.
